title.en: Volume 51 Treatises 32: Selection of Officials 1 - Jinshi in all Subjects and Legal Articles; Children Passing Examinations; Processes for Selecting Talented People; Successful Candidates in the Military Examinations; Institutions Administering Examinations; Astronomy Bureau; Examinations for Medicine
title.raw: 卷五十一 志第三十二: 選舉一 進士諸科律科 經童科 制舉 武舉 試學士院官 司天、醫學試科 Volume 51 Treatises 32: Selection of Officials 1 - Jinshi in all Subjects and Legal Articles; Children Passing Examinations; Processes for Selecting Talented People; Successful Candidates in the Military Examinations; Institutions Administering Examinations; Astronomy Bureau; Examinations for Medicine

sentences.zh: 進士諸科

translations.literal: The Jinshi and Related Degrees
translations.idiomatic: The Jinshi and Related Degrees

sentences.zh: 自三代鄉舉裏選之法廢，秦、漢以來各因一代之宜，以盡一時之才，苟足於用即已，故法度之不一，其來遠矣！

translations.literal: Since the methods of village recommendation and district selection of the Three Dynasties were abandoned, from Qin and Han onward each age adapted to its own needs to exhaust the talent of the time; if it sufficed for use, that was enough. Thus the lack of uniformity in regulations has a long history!
translations.idiomatic: After the village-recommendation and district-selection system of the Three Dynasties fell away, Qin and Han and every dynasty since shaped recruitment to its own needs, drawing on whatever talent the age could supply. Standards have never been uniform, and that divergence reaches far back into antiquity.

sentences.zh: 在漢之世，雖有賢良方正諸科以取士，而推擇為吏，由是以致公卿，公卿子弟入備宿衛，因被寵遇，以位通顯。

translations.literal: In the Han age, although there were such categories as Worthy and Upright and Rectified to select scholars, promotion and selection as clerks led thereby to the ranks of chief ministers; the sons of chief ministers entered service as palace guards, and through favored treatment attained conspicuous rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, categories such as Worthy and Upright and Rectified did recruit men of learning, yet the usual path was selection as a clerk, then advancement to the highest offices. Sons of grandees entered the palace guard, won imperial favor, and rose to eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉而下互有因革，至於唐、宋，進士盛焉。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin downward there were successive reforms, and by Tang and Song the jinshi degree flourished.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward each dynasty revised the system in turn; by Tang and Song the jinshi track had become paramount.

sentences.zh: 當時士君子之進，不由是塗則自以為慊，此由時君之好尚，故人心之趣向然也。

translations.literal: At that time gentlemen who advanced not by this path felt themselves deficient; this arose from what the rulers of the age favored, and so the bent of men's minds followed.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman who did not advance by that route felt himself at a disadvantage, for rulers set the fashion and scholars followed where favor pointed.

sentences.zh: 遼起唐季，頗用唐進士法取人，然仕于其國者，考其致身之所自，進士才十之二三耳！

translations.literal: The Liao arose in the late Tang and largely used Tang jinshi methods to recruit men, yet among those who served in that state, examining where they had risen from, jinshi were only two or three in ten!
translations.idiomatic: The Liao rose in the late Tang and largely adopted Tang jinshi recruitment, yet among officials in that realm only two or three in ten had actually entered service through the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 金承遼後，凡事欲軼遼世，故進士科目兼采唐、宋之法而增損之。

translations.literal: The Jin succeeded the Liao; in all matters they wished to surpass the Liao age, and so in jinshi subjects they drew on Tang and Song methods together and added or subtracted from them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin succeeded the Liao and sought in every respect to outdo their predecessors, so the jinshi curriculum combined Tang and Song models with Jin adjustments.

sentences.zh: 其及第出身，視前代特重，而法亦密焉。

translations.literal: Passing the examinations and taking office was regarded as especially weighty compared with earlier dynasties, and the regulations were also strict.
translations.idiomatic: Graduation and initial appointment carried greater prestige than in earlier dynasties, and the rules governing them were tighter.

sentences.zh: 若夫以策論進士取其國人，而用女直文字以為程文，斯蓋就其所長以收其用，又欲行其國字，使人通習而不廢耳。

translations.literal: As for selecting their own people through policy-essay jinshi and using Jurchen script for examination papers, this was surely to take what they excelled at and put it to use, and also to circulate their national script so that men would master it and it would not fall into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: The policy-essay jinshi track recruited Jurchen subjects in their own script both to employ native strengths and to keep the national writing in daily use so it would not die out.

sentences.zh: 終金之代，科目得人為盛。

translations.literal: Throughout the Jin age, the examination subjects produced men in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Through the whole Jin period the examination system supplied the state with talent in remarkable numbers.

sentences.zh: 諸宮護衛、及省台部譯史、令史、通事、仕進皆列于正班，斯則唐、宋以來之所無者，豈非因時制宜，而以漢法為依據者乎？

translations.literal: Palace guards of all ranks, as well as translators, clerks, and interpreters of the provincial and central ministries who entered service were all ranked in the regular sequence—something without precedent since Tang and Song. Was this not adapting to the times on the basis of Han methods?
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards, ministry translators, clerks, and interpreters who entered service were all placed in the regular civil ranks—something Tang and Song had never done. It was adaptation to circumstance, with Han institutions as the model.

sentences.zh: 金治純駁，議者於是每有別焉。

translations.literal: Jin governance was mixed in quality, and commentators on this point often drew distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Jin administration was uneven in quality, and commentators have long debated the point.

sentences.zh: 宣宗南渡，吏習日盛，苛刻成風，殆亦多故之秋，急於事功，不免爾歟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong crossed south, clerical practice grew daily, and harshness became the fashion—perhaps in that season of many troubles, urgency for results could not be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanzong moved the court south, bureaucratic routine thickened and harshness became habitual—perhaps inevitable in troubled times when quick results were demanded.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，仕進之歧既廣，僥倖之俗益熾，軍伍勞效，雜置令祿，門廕右職，迭居朝著，科舉取士亦複氾濫，而金治衰矣！

translations.literal: From that time onward the paths to office widened, the custom of lucky chance grew hotter, military service and merit were mixed with civil salaries, hereditary privilege for high offices filled the court in turn, and examination recruitment also became diluted—and Jin rule declined!
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter routes to office multiplied, opportunism flourished, military merit bought civil salaries, hereditary privilege crowded the court, and the examinations themselves were debased—after which Jin governance declined.

sentences.zh: 原其立經陳紀之初，所為升轉之格，考察之方，井井然有條而不紊，百有餘年才具不乏，豈非其效乎？

translations.literal: Tracing back to when they first established their institutions and laid down their standards, the rules for promotion and transfer and the methods of evaluation were orderly and without confusion; for more than a hundred years supplies did not run short—was this not their effect?
translations.idiomatic: At the founding, promotion rules and evaluation procedures were clear and coherent; for more than a century the state never lacked qualified men—surely that was the system's reward.

sentences.zh: 奉詔作《金史》，志其《選舉》，因得而詳論之，司天、太醫、內侍等法歷代所有，附著於斯。

translations.literal: By imperial order we compile the History of Jin and record Selection and Appointment in a treatise, and so may discuss it in detail; methods for astronomy, medicine, palace service, and the like, which every dynasty has had, are appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compile the History of Jin, we treat Selection and Appointment at length here, with astronomical, medical, and palace-service examinations—which every dynasty maintained—appended in the same chapter.

sentences.zh: 鬻爵、進納，金季之弊莫甚焉，蓋由財用之不足而然也，特載《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Selling offices and paying for entry were the greatest abuses of the late Jin, arising from insufficient revenue; they are recorded separately in the Treatise on Food and Goods.
translations.idiomatic: Sale of offices and paid admission were the worst abuses of late Jin, born of fiscal shortfall; they are treated in the Treatise on Food and Goods.

sentences.zh: 金設科皆因遼、宋制，有詞賦、經義、策試、律科、經童之制海陵天德三年，罷策試科。

translations.literal: The Jin established subjects all following Liao and Song systems: there were regulations for rhapsody, classical exegesis, policy examination, legal studies, and child classics. In Tiande 3 under Prince Hailing, the policy-examination subject was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jin examination subjects followed Liao and Song precedent: rhapsody, classical exegesis, policy tests, legal studies, and child classics. In Hailing's Tiande 3 (1155) the policy-examination track was abolished.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定十一年，創設女直進士科，初但試策，後增試論，所謂策論進士也。

translations.literal: In Dading 11 under Emperor Shizong, the Jurchen jinshi subject was first created; at first only policy questions were tested, and later essays were added—the so-called policy-essay jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizong's Dading 11 (1171) the court created the Jurchen jinshi degree, first testing policy questions alone and later adding essays—the policy-essay jinshi.

sentences.zh: 明昌初，又設制舉宏詞科，以待非常之士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingchang, the special recruitment and eloquence subject was also established to await extraordinary scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Mingchang era (1190) the court added a special recruitment track in polished composition for exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 故金取士之目有七焉。

translations.literal: Thus the categories by which the Jin recruited scholars were seven in number.
translations.idiomatic: In all, the Jin recruited through seven examination categories.

sentences.zh: 其試詞賦、經義、策論中選者，謂之進士。

translations.literal: Those who passed the rhapsody, classical exegesis, and policy-essay examinations were called jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who passed the rhapsody, classical exegesis, or policy-essay examinations were called jinshi.

sentences.zh: 律科、經童中選者，曰舉人。

translations.literal: Those who passed legal studies and child classics were called juren.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed legal studies or the child-classics examination were called juren.

sentences.zh: 凡養士之地曰國子監，始置於天德三年，後定制，詞賦、經義生百人，小學生百人，以宗室及外戚皇后大功以上親、諸功臣及三品以上官兄弟子孫，年十五以上者入學，不及十五者入小學。

translations.literal: Places for nurturing scholars were called the Directorate of Education, first established in Tiande 3; later fixed regulations set rhapsody and classical-exegesis students at one hundred and elementary students at one hundred. Imperial clansmen, consort kin within the mourning grade of great merit and above, sons and grandsons of meritorious officials and of officials of the third rank and above who were fifteen or older entered the main school; those not yet fifteen entered the elementary school.
translations.idiomatic: Schools for training scholars were headed by the Directorate of Education, founded in Tiande 3. Under later rules it enrolled one hundred rhapsody and exegesis students and one hundred elementary pupils: imperial clansmen, consort kin within the great-merit mourning circle, and sons and grandsons of meritorious officials or officials of rank 3 and above entered at age fifteen; younger boys entered the elementary division.

sentences.zh: 大定六年始置太學，初養士百六十人，後定五品以上官兄弟子孫百五十人，曾得府薦及終場人二百五十人，凡四百人。

translations.literal: In Dading 6 the Imperial University was first established, initially nurturing one hundred sixty scholars; later it was fixed at one hundred fifty sons and grandsons of officials of the fifth rank and above, and two hundred fifty who had received prefectural recommendation or completed the full examination cycle—four hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University was founded in Dading 6 (1166), first with 160 students; later quotas fixed 150 places for sons and grandsons of officials of rank 5 and above and 250 for men with prefectural recommendations or who had completed a full examination cycle—400 in total.

sentences.zh: 府學亦大定十六年置，凡十七處，共千人。

translations.literal: Prefectural schools were also established in Dading 16, seventeen in all, totaling one thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural schools were added in Dading 16 (1176): seventeen institutions with one thousand students altogether.

sentences.zh: 初以嘗與廷試及宗室皇家袒免以上親、並得解舉人為之。

translations.literal: At first those who had taken the palace examination, imperial clansmen and royal kin within the grade of mourning when the upper garment is removed, and juren who had received release were admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Initially enrollment was limited to men who had sat the palace examination, imperial clansmen and royal kin within the upper-garment mourning circle, and juren who had passed the qualifying round.

sentences.zh: 後增州學，遂加以五品以上官、曾任隨朝六品官之兄弟子孫，余官之兄弟子孫經府薦者，同境內舉人試補三之一，闕里廟宅子孫年十三以上不限數，經府薦及終場免試者不得過二十人。

translations.literal: Later prefectural schools were added, and there were further included sons and grandsons of officials of the fifth rank and above and of officials who had served at court in the sixth rank; for other officials' sons and grandsons with prefectural recommendation, one-third of juren within the same jurisdiction were admitted by examination; descendants of the Confucian temple estate aged thirteen and above were unlimited in number; those with prefectural recommendation and full examination completion who were exempt from testing could not exceed twenty.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectural schools were added, sons and grandsons of officials of rank 5 and above and of former sixth-rank court officials were admitted, along with other officials' kin on prefectural nomination; one-third of local juren could enter by examination; descendants of the Confucian temple estate aged thirteen or older were unlimited; and no more than twenty men with prefectural recommendation who had completed the full examination cycle could enter without testing.

sentences.zh: 凡試補學生，太學則禮部主之，州府則以提舉學校學官主之，曾得府薦及終場舉人，皆免試。

translations.literal: For all trial admission of students, the Imperial University was supervised by the Ministry of Rites, and prefectures and circuits by the officials who supervised schools; those who had received prefectural recommendation and juren who had completed the full cycle were all exempt from testing.
translations.idiomatic: Trial admission to schools was run by the Ministry of Rites for the Imperial University and by school superintendents in prefectures and circuits; men with prefectural recommendations or who had completed the full examination cycle were exempt.

sentences.zh: 凡經，《易》則用王弼、韓康伯注，《書》用孔安國注，《詩》用毛萇注、鄭玄箋，《春秋左氏傳》用杜預注，《禮記》用孔穎達疏，《周禮》用鄭玄注、賈公彥疏，《論語》用何晏集注。

translations.literal: For the Classics: the Changes used the commentaries of Wang Bi and Han Kangbo; the Documents the commentary of Kong Anguo; the Odes the commentary of Mao Chang and the notes of Zheng Xuan; the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn the commentary of Du Yu; the Record of Rites the subcommentary of Kong Yingda; the Rites of Zhou the commentary of Zheng Xuan and the subcommentary of Jia Gongyan; the Analects the collected commentary of He Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The curriculum used standard commentaries: Wang Bi and Han Kangbo on the Changes, Kong Anguo on the Documents, Mao Chang and Zheng Xuan on the Odes, Du Yu on the Zuo Commentary, Kong Yingda on the Record of Rites, Zheng Xuan and Jia Gongyan on the Rites of Zhou, and He Yan's collected notes on the Analects.

sentences.zh: 邢昺疏，《孟子》用趙岐注，孫奭疏，《孝經》用唐玄宗注，《史記》用裴駰注，《前漢書》用顏師古注。

translations.literal: Xing Bing's subcommentary; Mencius used Zhao Qi's commentary and Sun Shi's subcommentary; the Classic of Filial Piety used Emperor Xuanzong of Tang's commentary; the Records of the Grand Historian used Pei Yin; the History of the Former Han used Yan Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Bing's subcommentary was used where applicable; Mencius followed Zhao Qi with Sun Shi's subcommentary; the Classic of Filial Piety used Tang Xuanzong's commentary; the Grand Historian Pei Yin; the Former Han Yan Shigu.

sentences.zh: 《後漢書》用李賢注，《三國志》用裴松之注，及唐太宗《晉書》、沈約《宋書》，蕭子顯《齊書》、姚思廉《梁書》《陳書》、魏收《後魏書》、李百藥《北齊書》、令狐德棻《周書》、魏征《隋書》、新舊《唐書》、新舊《五代史》，《老子》用唐玄宗注疏，《荀子》用楊倞注，《揚子》用李軌、宋鹹、柳宗元、吳秘注，皆自國子監印之，授諸學校。

translations.literal: The History of the Later Han used Li Xian's commentary; the Records of the Three Kingdoms Pei Songzhi's; as well as Emperor Taizong of Tang's Book of Jin, Shen Yue's Book of Song, Xiao Zixian's Book of Qi, Yao Silian's Books of Liang and Chen, Wei Shou's Book of Later Wei, Li Baiyao's Book of Northern Qi, Linghu Defen's Book of Zhou, Wei Zheng's Book of Sui, the old and new Books of Tang, and the old and new Histories of the Five Dynasties; the Laozi used Emperor Xuanzong of Tang's commentary and subcommentary; the Xunzi Yang Liang's; the Yangzi the commentaries of Li Gui, Song Xian, Liu Zongyuan, and Wu Bi—all were printed by the Directorate and distributed to the schools.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han used Li Xian; Three Kingdoms Pei Songzhi; standard dynastic histories from Jin through the Five Dynasties; Laozi Tang Xuanzong's commentary; Xunzi Yang Liang; Yangzi the notes of Li Gui, Song Xian, Liu Zongyuan, and Wu Bi—all printed by the Directorate and issued to every school.

sentences.zh: 凡學生會課，三日作策論一道，又三日作賦及詩各一篇，三月一私試，以季月初先試賦，間一日試策論，中選者以上五名申部。

translations.literal: For all students' regular lessons, every three days one policy essay was written, and every three days thereafter one rhapsody and one poem; every three months a private examination was held, at the beginning of each season first testing rhapsody, and after one day testing policy essays; those who passed reported the top five names to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Students wrote one policy essay every three days and one rhapsody plus one poem in the next three-day cycle. Every quarter they took a private exam: rhapsody on the first day of the season, policy essay the day after; the top five passes were reported to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 遇旬休、節辰皆有假，病則給假，省親遠行則給程。

translations.literal: On decad rest days and festival dates there were holidays; for illness leave was granted; for visiting kin on distant journeys travel time was allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Decad holidays and festival days were days off; sick leave was granted; long journeys to visit family received official travel time.

sentences.zh: 犯學規者罰，不率教者黜。

translations.literal: Those who violated school regulations were punished; those who did not follow instruction were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Violations of school rules brought punishment; persistent failure to follow instruction brought dismissal.

sentences.zh: 遭喪百日後求入學者，不得與釋奠禮。

translations.literal: Those who after a hundred days of mourning sought to enter the school could not take part in the libation ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Students who re-entered after the hundred-day mourning period could not participate in the libation ceremony.

sentences.zh: 凡國子學生三年不能充貢，欲就諸局承應者，學官試，能粗通大小各一經者聽。

translations.literal: For all Directorate students who after three years could not qualify for tribute, if they wished to take posts as clerks in the various bureaus, the school officials tested them; those who could roughly master one classic from the greater and one from the lesser set were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Directorate students who failed to qualify for the examinations within three years might, if they wished clerkships in government bureaus, sit a school examination; those with rough mastery of one major and one minor classic were allowed to proceed.

sentences.zh: 章宗大定二十九年，上封事者乞興學校，推行三舍法，及鄉以八行貢春官，以設制舉宏詞。

translations.literal: In Dading 29 under Emperor Zhangzong, memorialists asked to expand schools, implement the three-dormitory method, and recommend men to the Ministry of Rites by the eight conduct categories from the districts, and to establish the special recruitment and eloquence subject.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhangzong's Dading 29 (1189) memorialists urged wider schools, adoption of the Song three-dormitory system, district recommendation by the eight conduct virtues, and a special eloquence examination.

sentences.zh: 事下尚書省集百官議，戶部尚書鄧儼等謂：「三舍之法起于宋熙寧間，王安石罷詩賦，專尚經術。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Secretariat to assemble officials for discussion. Minister of Revenue Deng Yan and others said: 'The three-dormitory method arose in the Xining era of Song; Wang Anshi abolished poetry and rhapsody and honored classical learning alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat convened officials for debate. Minister of Revenue Deng Yan and others argued: 'The three-dormitory system began in Song's Xining reforms, when Wang Anshi abolished poetry and rhapsody in favor of classical learning alone.

sentences.zh: 太學生初補外舍，無定員。

translations.literal: Imperial University students were first placed in the outer dormitory, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Students first entered the outer dormitory without a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 由外升內舍，限二百人。

translations.literal: From the outer they advanced to the inner dormitory, limited to two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion from outer to inner dormitory was capped at two hundred.

sentences.zh: 由內升上舍，限百人。

translations.literal: From the inner they advanced to the upper dormitory, limited to one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion from inner to upper dormitory was capped at one hundred.

sentences.zh: 各治一經，每月考試，或特免解，或保舉補官。

translations.literal: Each studied one classic, with monthly examinations; some received special exemption from the qualifying round, or recommendation for office.
translations.idiomatic: Each student mastered one classic under monthly exams, with some winning exemption from the qualifying round or direct recommendation to office.

sentences.zh: 其法雖行，而多席勢力、尚趨走之弊，故蘇軾有'三舍既興，貨賂公行'之語，是以元祐間罷之，後雖複，而宣和三年竟廢。

translations.literal: Although the method was implemented, it largely relied on power and favored those skilled in currying favor; hence Su Shi had the saying 'Once the three dormitories arose, bribes went openly,' and so in the Yuanyou era it was abolished; though later restored, in Xuanhe 3 it was finally discarded.
translations.idiomatic: Though implemented, the system favored influence and flattery; Su Shi remarked that once the three dormitories existed, bribery ran openly. Yuanyou abolished it; it was briefly restored but finally discarded in Xuanhe 3 (1121).

sentences.zh: 臣等謂立法貴乎可久，彼三舍之法委之學官選試，啟僥倖之門，不可為法。

translations.literal: We consider that in making laws what is valued is durability; that three-dormitory method, leaving selection to school officials, opens the gate to lucky chance and cannot serve as law.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that laws should endure. Entrusting advancement to school officials, as the three-dormitory system did, invites opportunism and should not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 唐文皇養士至八千人，亡宋兩學五千人，今策論、詞賦、經義三科取士，而太學所養止百六十人，外京府或至十人，天下僅及千人。

translations.literal: Tang Taizong nurtured scholars up to eight thousand; the fallen Song's two schools had five thousand; today the three subjects of policy essay, rhapsody, and classical exegesis recruit scholars, yet the Imperial University nurtures only one hundred sixty, and outer capital prefectures sometimes only ten—the empire barely reaches one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Taizong supported eight thousand students; the defunct Song's two capitals enrolled five thousand; yet Jin's three examination tracks feed an Imperial University of only 160, with some outer capitals enrolling as few as ten—barely a thousand students empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 今若每州設學，專除教授，月加考試，每舉所取數多者賞其學官。

translations.literal: If now each prefecture established a school, appointed instructors exclusively, added monthly examinations, and rewarded school officials whose districts produced the most passes each round,
translations.idiomatic: If every prefecture had its own school with dedicated instructors, monthly exams, and rewards for officials whose districts produced the most graduates each cycle,

sentences.zh: 月試定為三等籍之，一歲中頻在上等者優複之，不率教、行惡者黜之，庶幾得人之道也。

translations.literal: monthly tests were fixed in three grades and recorded; those frequently in the upper grade within a year received preferential treatment; those who did not follow instruction or whose conduct was bad were dismissed—then perhaps the way of obtaining men would be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: with monthly results recorded in three grades, frequent top performers rewarded, and the disobedient or vicious dismissed, the state might truly secure talent.

sentences.zh: 又成周鄉舉裏選法卒不可複，設科取士各隨其時。

translations.literal: Moreover, the village recommendation and district selection of the accomplished Zhou could in the end not be restored; establishing subjects to recruit scholars should each follow its own time.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou village-recommendation system cannot be revived; each age must shape recruitment to its own needs.

sentences.zh: 八行者乃亡宋取《周禮》之六行孝、友、睦、姻、任、恤，加之中、和為八也。

translations.literal: The eight conduct categories were taken by the fallen Song from the six conduct categories of the Rites of Zhou—filial piety, friendship, harmony, marriage ties, responsibility, and compassion—with centrality and harmony added to make eight.
translations.idiomatic: The eight conduct virtues were a Song borrowing from the Zhou Rites—filial piety, friendship, harmony, marriage ties, responsibility, and compassion—plus centrality and harmony to make eight.

sentences.zh: 凡人之行莫大于孝廉，今已有舉孝廉之法，及民有才能德行者令縣官薦之。

translations.literal: Among human conduct nothing is greater than filial integrity; today there is already a method for recommending filial and upright men, and when the people have talent, ability, and virtuous conduct the county officials are ordered to recommend them.
translations.idiomatic: No virtue exceeds filial integrity; Jin already recommends filial and upright men, and county officials are to nominate citizens of talent and good character.

sentences.zh: 今制，犯十惡奸盜者不得應試，亦六德六行之遺意也。

translations.literal: Under present regulations, those who commit the ten abominations or theft and treachery may not take the examinations—also a vestige of the six virtues and six conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Present rules bar examinees guilty of the ten abominations or theft and treachery—a remnant of the Zhou six virtues and six conduct.

sentences.zh: 夫制舉宏詞，蓋天子待非常之士，若設此科，不限進士，並選人試之，中選擢之台閣，則人自勉矣。

translations.literal: As for special recruitment and eloquence, it is how the Son of Heaven awaits extraordinary scholars; if this subject were established, not limiting it to jinshi but also testing selectees, and promoting those who passed to the central ministries, then men would encourage themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Special eloquence examinations are how the throne seeks extraordinary talent. If opened to jinshi and selectees alike, with passes promoted to central office, men would strive on their own.

sentences.zh: 」上從其議。

translations.literal: ' The emperor followed their proposal.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor accepted their proposal.

sentences.zh: 遂計州府戶口。

translations.literal: Thereupon household registers of prefectures and circuits were tallied.
translations.idiomatic: The court then tallied prefectural household registers.

sentences.zh: 增養士之數，於大定舊制京府十七處千人之外，置節鎮、防禦州學六十處，增養千人。

translations.literal: The number of scholars nurtured was increased; beyond the thousand at seventeen capital prefectures under the old Dading system, sixty military-commission and defense-prefecture schools were established, adding one thousand nurtured scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Enrollment was expanded: beyond the thousand students at seventeen capital prefectures under the old Dading quotas, sixty schools at military commissions and defense prefectures added another thousand.

sentences.zh: 各設教授一員，選五舉終場或進士年五十以上者為之。

translations.literal: Each was given one instructor, chosen from those who had completed five examination rounds or jinshi aged fifty and above.
translations.idiomatic: Each school received one instructor, chosen from men who had completed five examination cycles or jinshi aged fifty or older.

sentences.zh: 府學二十有四，學生九百五人。

translations.literal: There were twenty-four prefectural schools, with nine hundred five students.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four prefectural schools enrolled 905 students.

sentences.zh: 大興、開封、平陽、真定、東平府各六十人，太原、益都府各五十人，大定、河間、濟南、大名、京兆府各四十人，遼陽、彰德府各三十人，河中、慶陽、臨洮、河南府各二十五人，鳳翔、平涼、延安、咸平、廣寧、興中府各二十人。

translations.literal: Daxing, Kaifeng, Pingyang, Zhending, and Dongping Prefectures each sixty; Taiyuan and Yidu Prefectures each fifty; Dading, Hejian, Jinan, Daming, and Jingzhao Prefectures each forty; Liaoyang and Zhangde Prefectures each thirty; Hezhong, Qingyang, Lintao, and Henan Prefectures each twenty-five; Fengxiang, Pingliang, Yan'an, Xianping, Guangning, and Xingzhong Prefectures each twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Daxing, Kaifeng, Pingyang, Zhending, and Dongping enrolled 60 each; Taiyuan and Yidu 50; Dading, Hejian, Jinan, Daming, and Jingzhao 40; Liaoyang and Zhangde 30; Hezhong, Qingyang, Lintao, and Henan 25; Fengxiang, Pingliang, Yan'an, Xianping, Guangning, and Xingzhong 20.

sentences.zh: 節鎮學三十九，共六百一十五人。

translations.literal: There were thirty-nine military-commission schools, six hundred fifteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-nine military-commission schools enrolled 615 students.

sentences.zh: 絳、定、衛、懷、滄州各三十人，萊、密、潞、汾、冀、邢、兗州各二十五人，代、同、邠州各二十人，奉聖州十五人，餘二十三節鎮皆十人。

translations.literal: Jiang, Ding, Wei, Huai, and Cang Prefectures each thirty; Lai, Mi, Lu, Fen, Ji, Xing, and Yan Prefectures each twenty-five; Dai, Tong, and Bin Prefectures each twenty; Fengsheng Prefecture fifteen; the remaining twenty-three military commissions each ten.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, Ding, Wei, Huai, and Cang enrolled 30 each; Lai, Mi, Lu, Fen, Ji, Xing, and Yan 25; Dai, Tong, and Bin 20; Fengsheng 15; the other twenty-three commissions 10 each.

sentences.zh: 防禦州學二十一，共二百三十五人。

translations.literal: There were twenty-one defense-prefecture schools, two hundred thirty-five in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one defense-prefecture schools enrolled 235 students.

sentences.zh: 博、德、洺、棣、亳各十五人，餘十六州各十人。

translations.literal: Bo, De, Ming, Di, and Bo Prefectures each fifteen; the remaining sixteen prefectures each ten.
translations.idiomatic: Bo, De, Ming, Di, and Bo enrolled 15 each; the other sixteen defense prefectures 10 each.

sentences.zh: 凡千八百人。

translations.literal: In all one thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The total came to 1,800 students.

sentences.zh: 女直學。

translations.literal: Jurchen Schools
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen Schools

sentences.zh: 自大定四年，以女直大小字譯經書頒行之。

translations.literal: From Dading 4, the classics were translated into large and small Jurchen script and promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: From Dading 4 (1164) the classics were translated into large and small Jurchen script and issued.

sentences.zh: 後擇猛安謀克內良家子弟為學生，諸路至三千人。

translations.literal: Later sons of good families within the meng'an and mouke were chosen as students, reaching three thousand on all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Later sons of respectable families from the meng'an and mouke units were enrolled, reaching three thousand empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 九年，取其尤俊秀者百人至京師，以編修官溫蒂罕締達教之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the hundred most outstanding were taken to the capital and taught by the compilation official Wendihan Dida.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the hundred most promising students were brought to the capital and taught by compilation official Wendihan Dida.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以策、詩取士，始設女直國子學，諸路設女直府學，以新進士為教授。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year scholars were recruited by policy and poetry; the Jurchen Directorate school was first established, and Jurchen prefectural schools on all circuits, with newly made jinshi as instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year recruitment by policy essay and poetry began; the Jurchen Directorate and circuit prefectural schools were founded, staffed by newly minted jinshi.

sentences.zh: 國子學策論生百人，小學生百人。

translations.literal: The Directorate had one hundred policy-essay students and one hundred elementary students.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate enrolled one hundred policy-essay students and one hundred elementary pupils.

sentences.zh: 府州學二十二，中都、上京、胡裏改、恤頻、合懶、蒲與、婆速、咸平、泰州、臨潢、北京、冀州、開州、豐州、西京、東京、蓋州、隆州、東平、益都、河南、陝西置之。

translations.literal: There were twenty-two prefectural and circuit schools, established at Zhongdu, Shangjing, Hurigai, Xupin, Helan, Puyu, Posu, Xianping, Taizhou, Linhuang, Beijing, Jizhou, Kaizhou, Fengzhou, Xijing, Dongjing, Gaizhou, Longzhou, Dongping, Yidu, Henan, and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-two prefectural schools were established at Zhongdu, Shangjing, Hurigai, Xupin, Helan, Puyu, Posu, Xianping, Taizhou, Linhuang, Beijing, Jizhou, Kaizhou, Fengzhou, Xijing, Dongjing, Gaizhou, Longzhou, Dongping, Yidu, Henan, and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 凡取國子學生、府學生之制，皆與詞賦、經義生同。

translations.literal: For all regulations on admitting Directorate and prefectural students, they were the same as for rhapsody and classical-exegesis students.
translations.idiomatic: Admission rules for Directorate and prefectural Jurchen students matched those for Han rhapsody and exegesis students.

sentences.zh: 又定制，每謀克取二人，若宗室每二十戶內無願學者，則取有物力家子弟年十三以上、二十以下者充。

translations.literal: Further regulations were fixed: two were taken from each mouke; if within every twenty imperial-clan households none wished to study, then sons of property-owning families aged thirteen and above and twenty and below were taken to fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations fixed two students per mouke; if no clansman within twenty households wished to study, sons of property-owning families aged thirteen to twenty filled the places.

sentences.zh: 凡會課，三日作策論一道，季月私試如漢生制。

translations.literal: For all regular lessons, every three days one policy essay was written; quarterly private examinations followed the Han-student system.
translations.idiomatic: Lessons required one policy essay every three days; quarterly private exams followed the same schedule as for Han students.

sentences.zh: 大定二十九年，敕凡京府鎮州諸學，各以女直、漢人進士長貳官提控其事，具入官銜。

translations.literal: In Dading 29 an edict ordered that for all schools in capital prefectures and military commissions, Jurchen and Han jinshi in senior and junior posts should supervise the matter, with their official titles recorded.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29 (1189) the throne ordered capital and commission schools supervised by senior Jurchen and Han jinshi, with their titles formally recorded.

sentences.zh: 河南、陝西女直學，承安二年罷之，餘如舊。

translations.literal: Jurchen schools in Henan and Shaanxi were abolished in Chengan 2; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen schools in Henan and Shaanxi were closed in Chengan 2 (1197); elsewhere the system continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 凡諸進士舉人，由鄉至府，由府至省，及殿廷，凡四試皆中選，則官之。

translations.literal: For all jinshi and juren, from the district to the prefecture, from the prefecture to the province, and to the palace hall—in all four examinations, if they passed they were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi and juren advanced through district, prefectural, provincial, and palace examinations; passing all four brought appointment.

sentences.zh: 至廷試五被黜，則賜之第，謂之恩例。

translations.literal: If at the palace examination they were rejected five times, a degree was bestowed—called the grace precedent.
translations.idiomatic: After five failures at the palace examination, candidates received a conferred degree—the grace precedent.

sentences.zh: 又有特命及第者，謂之特恩。

translations.literal: There were also those who passed by special order—called special grace.
translations.idiomatic: Some passed by special imperial order—special grace.

sentences.zh: 恩例者但考文之高下為第，而不復黜落。

translations.literal: For grace precedent, only the quality of the writing was graded for ranking, and there was no further rejection.
translations.idiomatic: Under the grace precedent, candidates were ranked by writing quality alone, with no further elimination.

sentences.zh: 凡詞賦進士，試賦、詩、策論各一道。

translations.literal: For all rhapsody jinshi, one rhapsody, one poem, and one policy essay were tested.
translations.idiomatic: Rhapsody jinshi candidates wrote one rhapsody, one poem, and one policy essay.

sentences.zh: 經義進士，試所治一經義、策論各一道。

translations.literal: Classical-exegesis jinshi were tested on exegesis of the one classic they studied and one policy essay each.
translations.idiomatic: Classical-exegesis jinshi wrote exegesis on their chosen classic and one policy essay.

sentences.zh: 其設也，始于太宗天會元年十一月，時以急欲得漢士以撫輯新附，初無定數，亦無定期，故二年二月、八月凡再行焉。

translations.literal: Its establishment began in the eleventh month of Tianhui 1 under Emperor Taizong; at that time, eager to obtain Han scholars to pacify the newly submitted, there was initially no fixed quota and no fixed schedule, and so in the second year it was held again in the second and eighth months.
translations.idiomatic: The system began in Taizong's Tianhui 1 (1123), month 11, when the court urgently sought Han scholars to govern newly submitted territories. With no fixed quotas or schedule, examinations were held again in months 2 and 8 of the following year.

sentences.zh: 五年，以河北、河東初降，職員多闕，以遼、宋之制不同，詔南北各因其素所習之業取士，號為南北選。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because Hebei and Hedong had newly submitted and offices were many in vacancy, and Liao and Song systems differed, an edict ordered north and south each to recruit scholars according to the occupations they were accustomed to—called the north-south selection.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, with Hebei and Hedong newly subdued and offices vacant, and Liao and Song customs differing, the court ordered separate north and south recruitment by local specialty—the north-south selection.

sentences.zh: 熙宗天眷元年五月，詔南北選各以經義、詞賦兩科取士。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Tianjuan 1 under Emperor Xizong, an edict ordered north and south selections each to recruit by the two subjects of classical exegesis and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xizong's Tianjuan 1 (1138), north and south selections were each ordered to recruit through classical exegesis and rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 海陵庶人天德二年，始增殿試之制，而更定試期。

translations.literal: In Tiande 2 under the commoner Prince Hailing, the palace-examination system was first added and the examination schedule was revised.
translations.idiomatic: In Hailing's Tiande 2 (1150) the palace examination was introduced and the examination calendar fixed.

sentences.zh: 三年，並南北選為一，罷經義、策試兩科，專以詞賦取士。

translations.literal: In the third year north and south selections were merged into one; the subjects of classical exegesis and policy examination were abolished, and recruitment relied solely on rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year north and south selections were merged; classical exegesis and policy tests were abolished, and recruitment relied on rhapsody alone.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，定貢舉程試條理格法。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuan 1 the regulations and methods for tribute recruitment and examination procedures were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan 1 (1153) codified the rules governing tribute recruitment and examinations.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年，命以《五經》、《三史》正文內出題，始定為三年一辟。

translations.literal: In Zhenglong 1 it was ordered that questions be drawn from the main text of the Five Classics and Three Histories, and the cycle was first fixed at once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglong 1 (1156) required questions drawn from the Five Classics and Three Histories and fixed the examination cycle at once every three years.

sentences.zh: 大定四年，敕宰臣：「進士文優則取，勿限人數。

translations.literal: In Dading 4 the chief ministers were commanded: 'If jinshi writings are excellent, take them; do not limit the number.'
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 4 (1164) the emperor told his ministers: 'Recruit every jinshi candidate whose writing is excellent; impose no quota.'

sentences.zh: 」十八年，謂宰臣：「文士有偶中魁選，不問操履，而輒授翰苑之職。

translations.literal: ' In the eighteenth year he told the chief ministers: 'There are literati who by chance top the selection; without inquiring into conduct they are forthwith given posts in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the eighteenth year he told his ministers: 'Some scholars win the top place by chance and, without inquiry into character, are posted straight to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 如趙承元，朕聞其無士行，果敗露。

translations.literal: Such as Zhao Chengyuan—I heard he lacked the conduct of a gentleman, and it was indeed exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chengyuan was one: I had heard he lacked scholarly character, and he was indeed exposed.

sentences.zh: 自今榜首，先訪察其鄉行，可取則授以應奉，否則從常調。

translations.literal: From now on, for top graduates, first investigate their conduct in their home district; if acceptable, grant them attendant service, otherwise follow the regular assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth top graduates must first be investigated for local reputation; the worthy receive attendant posts, the rest regular assignments.

sentences.zh: 」十九年，謂宰臣曰：「自來禦試賦題，皆士人嘗擬作者。

translations.literal: ' In the nineteenth year he told the chief ministers: 'From of old the rhapsody topics of the imperial examination were all ones scholars had already drafted.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the nineteenth year he said: 'Palace examination rhapsody topics were always ones candidates had already practiced.

sentences.zh: 前朕自選一題，出人所不料，故中選者多名士，而庸才不及焉。

translations.literal: Previously I myself chose one topic, unexpected to others; therefore those who passed were mostly eminent scholars, and mediocre talent did not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Once I chose my own topic, unforeseen by the candidates; the passes were mostly eminent scholars, and mediocrities fell short.

sentences.zh: 是知題難則名儒亦擅場，題易則庸流易僥倖也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that when topics are hard, even famous Confucians excel; when topics are easy, the mediocre easily gain lucky success.
translations.idiomatic: Hard topics let even great scholars shine; easy topics let mediocrities slip through by luck.

sentences.zh: 」平章政事唐括安禮奏曰：「臣前日言，士人不以策論為意者，正為此爾。

translations.literal: ' Grand Councilor Tangqut Anli memorialized: 'Your servant spoke the other day that scholars do not take policy essays to heart—precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: ' Grand Councilor Tangqut Anli replied: 'As I said recently, scholars neglect policy essays for exactly this reason.

sentences.zh: 宜各場通考，選文理俱優者。

translations.literal: Each examination venue should test comprehensively and select those excellent in both literary and expository skill.'
translations.idiomatic: Every stage of the examination should test comprehensively and select candidates strong in both literary and expository skill.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「並答時務策，觀其議論，材自可見，卿等其議之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor said: 'Let them all answer current-affairs policy questions; observing their discourse, talent will naturally appear. You ministers, deliberate on this.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor said: 'Require current-affairs policy essays as well; talent will show in the argument. Ministers, deliberate and report.'

sentences.zh: 」二十年，謂宰臣曰：「朕嘗諭進士不當限數，則對以所取之外無合格文，故中選者少，豈非題難致然耶？

translations.literal: ' In the twentieth year he told the chief ministers: 'I once instructed that jinshi should not be limited in number, and the reply was that beyond those taken there was no qualified writing—hence few passed. Was this not because the topics were difficult?'
translations.idiomatic: ' In the twentieth year he said: 'When I ordered jinshi recruitment without quotas, ministers replied that few writings qualified—was that not because the topics were too hard?'

sentences.zh: 若果多合格，而有司妄黜之，甚非理也。

translations.literal: If in truth many were qualified and the officials wrongly rejected them, that would be very unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: If many candidates truly qualified and officials rejected them anyway, that would be wholly unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「古者鄉舉有行者，授以官。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'In antiquity those recommended from the districts for conduct were given office.
translations.idiomatic: ' He added: 'In antiquity men recommended from the districts for their conduct received office at once.

sentences.zh: 今其考滿，察鄉曲實行出倫者擢之。

translations.literal: Now when their term of evaluation is complete, investigate those whose actual conduct in their home district exceeds the norm and promote them.'
translations.idiomatic: Now, when their evaluation term ends, promote those whose conduct at home truly stands out.'

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「舊不選策，今兼選矣。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'Formerly policy essays were not selected; now they are included.
translations.idiomatic: ' He also said: 'We once ignored policy essays; now we weigh them as well.

sentences.zh: 然自今府會兩試不須試策，已中策後，則試以制策，試學士院官。

translations.literal: Yet from now on the prefectural and metropolitan rounds need not test policy essays; after passing policy essays, they are then tested with institutional policy questions for Hanlin Academy posts.'
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth prefectural and metropolitan rounds need not include policy essays; after candidates pass them, test institutional policy essays for Hanlin posts.'

sentences.zh: 」二十二年，謂宰臣曰：「漢進士魁，例授應奉，若行不副名，不習制誥之文者，即與外除。

translations.literal: ' In the twenty-second year he told the chief ministers: 'Han jinshi top graduates were customarily given attendant posts; if conduct did not match reputation, or they did not master edict-drafting prose, give them outside assignments at once.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the twenty-second year he told his ministers: 'Han jinshi top graduates customarily received attendant posts; if character did not match reputation or they could not draft edicts, assign them outside the capital at once.

sentences.zh: 」二十三年，謂宰臣曰：「漢進士，皇統間人材殆不復見，今應奉以授狀元，蓋循資爾。

translations.literal: ' In the twenty-third year he told the chief ministers: 'Han jinshi—talent like that of the Huangtong era is scarcely seen again; now attendant posts are given to top graduates, merely following seniority.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the twenty-third year he said: 'Han jinshi talent like that of the Huangtong era is rarely seen; attendant posts for top graduates now merely follow seniority.

sentences.zh: 制誥文字，各以職事鋪敘，皆有定式，故易。

translations.literal: Edict and proclamation texts each narrate according to official duties and all have fixed forms, and so are easy.
translations.idiomatic: Routine edicts follow fixed formulas keyed to each office and are easy to draft.

sentences.zh: 至撰赦詔，則鮮有能者。

translations.literal: But in composing amnesty edicts, few are capable.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty edicts, however, few can write well.

sentences.zh: 」參知政事粘哥斡特剌對曰：「舊人已登第尚為學不輟，今人一及第輒廢而不學，故爾。

translations.literal: ' Vice Councilor Niege Wotela replied: 'Men of old, even after passing the examinations, still did not cease study; men today, once they pass, at once abandon study—hence this.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Vice Councilor Niege Wotela replied: 'Earlier generations kept studying after passing; today candidates stop the moment they graduate—that is why.'

sentences.zh: 」上於聽政之隙，召參知政事張汝霖、翰林直學士李晏讀新進士所對策，至縣令闕員取之何道？

translations.literal: ' During a break in hearing affairs, the emperor summoned Vice Councilor Zhang Rulin and Hanlin Academician Li Yan to read the policy answers of new jinshi, down to the question: By what means should vacant county magistrate posts be filled?
translations.idiomatic: ' During a break in court business the emperor summoned Vice Councilor Zhang Rulin and Hanlin Academician Li Yan to read new jinshi policy essays, including one on how to fill vacant county magistrate posts.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕夙夜思此，未知所出。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I think on this day and night, and do not know the way out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'I think of this day and night and do not know the answer.

sentences.zh: 」晏對曰：「臣竊念久矣！

translations.literal: ' Yan replied: 'Your servant has long pondered this in private!
translations.idiomatic: ' Yan replied: 'I have pondered this for a long time!

sentences.zh: 國朝設科，始分南北兩選，北選詞賦進士擢第一百五十人，經義五十人，南選百五十人，計三百五十人。

translations.literal: When our dynasty established subjects, it first divided north and south selections; the north selection took one hundred fifty rhapsody jinshi and fifty classical-exegesis; the south selection one hundred fifty—three hundred fifty in all.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty first established examinations, north and south selections were separate: the north took 150 rhapsody jinshi and 50 exegesis graduates; the south 150—350 in all.

sentences.zh: 嗣場，北選詞賦進士七十人，經義三十人，南選百五十人，計二百五十人。

translations.literal: In the supplementary round, the north selection took seventy rhapsody jinshi and thirty classical-exegesis; the south selection one hundred fifty—two hundred fifty in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the supplementary round the north took 70 rhapsody jinshi and 30 exegesis graduates; the south 150—250 in all.

sentences.zh: 以入仕者多，故員不闕。

translations.literal: Because many entered service, posts were not vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Because many men entered service, posts were not left vacant.

sentences.zh: 其後南北通選，止設詞賦科，不過取六七十人，以入仕者少，故縣令員闕也。

translations.literal: Later north and south were combined, only the rhapsody subject was kept, and no more than sixty or seventy were taken; because few entered service, county magistrate posts were vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Later the selections were merged and only the rhapsody track remained, taking at most sixty or seventy men; too few entered service, and county magistrate posts went unfilled.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「自今文理可采者取之，毋限以數。

translations.literal: ' The emperor said: 'From now on take those whose literary and expository skill is acceptable; do not limit by number.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor said: 'From now on recruit every candidate whose writing is acceptable; impose no quota.'

sentences.zh: 」二十八年，複經義科。

translations.literal: ' In the twenty-eighth year the classical-exegesis subject was restored.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the twenty-eighth year the classical-exegesis subject was restored.

sentences.zh: 章宗明昌元年正月，言事者謂：「舉人四試而鄉試似為虛設，固當罷去。

translations.literal: In the first month of Mingchang 1 under Emperor Zhangzong, memorialists said: 'Juren take four examinations while the district examination seems a mere formality and should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhangzong's Mingchang 1 (1190), memorialists argued that juren sat four examinations while the district round was redundant and should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 其府會試乞十人取一人，可以群經出題，而注示本傳。

translations.literal: For prefectural and metropolitan examinations, request one in ten, with questions drawn from the classics and the source passage indicated.'
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and metropolitan exams should take one in ten, with questions drawn from the classics and the source passage noted.'

sentences.zh: 」上是其言，詔免鄉試，府試以五人取一人，仍令有司議外路添考試院，及群經出題之制。

translations.literal: ' The emperor approved and ordered the district examination abolished, prefectural examination one in five, and still ordered the officials to deliberate adding examination halls on outer circuits and the system of questions from the classics.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor agreed: district examinations were abolished, prefectural exams took one in five, and officials were ordered to plan added examination halls on outer circuits and rules for classical questions.

sentences.zh: 有司言：「會試所取之數，舊止五百人，比以世宗敕中格者取，乞依此制行之。

translations.literal: The officials said: 'The number taken at the metropolitan examination was formerly capped at five hundred; recently, following Emperor Shizong's command to take all who met the standard, we beg to follow that system.'
translations.idiomatic: Officials replied: 'Metropolitan examinations were formerly capped at 500; since Shizong ordered taking all who met standard, we ask to follow that rule.'

sentences.zh: 府試舊六處，中有地遠者，命特添三處，上京、咸平府路則試于遼陽，河東南北路則試于平陽，山東東路則試於益都。

translations.literal: There were formerly six prefectural examination sites; among them some regions were distant, and three additional sites were specially ordered: Shangjing and Xianping Circuit Route examined at Liaoyang; Hedong North and South Route at Pingyang; Shandong East Route at Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Six prefectural examination sites existed; three more were added for distant regions: Shangjing and Xianping circuit candidates tested at Liaoyang, Hedong north and south at Pingyang, Shandong east at Yidu.

sentences.zh: 以《六經》、《十七史》、《孝經》、《論語》、《孟子》、及《荀》、《揚》、《老子》內出題，皆命於題下注其本傳。

translations.literal: Questions were to be drawn from the Six Classics, Seventeen Histories, Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mencius, and Xunzi, Yangzi, and Laozi, and all were ordered to have the source passage noted beneath the question.
translations.idiomatic: Questions were drawn from the Six Classics, Seventeen Histories, Filial Piety, Analects, Mencius, Xunzi, Yangzi, and Laozi, with the source passage cited under each question.

sentences.zh: 」又諭有司曰：「舉人程文所用故事，恐考試官或遽不能憶，誤失人材，可自注出處，注字之誤，不在塗注乙之數。」

translations.literal: ' He also instructed the officials: 'Historical allusions in candidates' examination papers—examiners may suddenly fail to recall them and wrongly lose talent; candidates may annotate their sources themselves; errors in annotations do not count toward the limit on corrections.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He also told officials: 'Candidates may cite their own sources for historical allusions lest examiners forget references and reject good men; annotation errors do not count toward correction limits.'

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，敕官或職至五品者，直赴禦試。

translations.literal: In Mingchang 2 it was commanded that officials or posts of the fifth rank and above proceed directly to the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 2 (1191) officials of rank 5 and above were allowed to proceed directly to the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 四年，平章政事守貞言：「國家官人之路，惟女直、漢人進士得人居多。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Grand Councilor Shouzhen said: 'Among the state's paths to office, only Jurchen and Han jinshi yield the most capable men.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Grand Councilor Shouzhen said: 'Of all routes to office, Jurchen and Han jinshi supply the most capable officials.

sentences.zh: 諸司局承應，舊無出身，自大定後始敘使，至今鮮有可用者。

translations.literal: Clerks in the various bureaus formerly had no formal standing; from Dading onward they began to receive appointments, yet to this day few are usable.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau clerks formerly had no formal standing; since Dading they have received appointments, yet few prove useful.

sentences.zh: 近來放進士第數稍多，此舉更宜增取，若會試止以五百人為限，則廷試雖欲多取，不可得也。

translations.literal: Recently the number of jinshi degrees granted has grown somewhat; this examination should take more; if the metropolitan examination is capped at five hundred, then even if the palace examination wishes to take more, it cannot be obtained.'
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi degrees have lately increased; metropolitan exams should take more candidates. If the metropolitan round stays capped at 500, the palace examination cannot expand even when talent warrants it.'

sentences.zh: 」上乃詔有司，會試毋限人數，文合格則取。

translations.literal: ' The emperor then ordered the officials: metropolitan examination shall not limit numbers; if the writing qualifies, take them.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor ordered officials to impose no metropolitan quota—take every candidate whose writing qualified.

sentences.zh: 六年，言事者謂：「學者率恃有司全注本傳以示之，故不勉讀書，乞減子史注本傳之制。

translations.literal: In the sixth year memorialists said: 'Scholars generally rely on officials fully annotating source passages for them, and so do not urge themselves to read; we beg to reduce the system of annotating source passages for histories and masters.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year memorialists complained that scholars relied on full source citations from officials and stopped studying; they asked to reduce citations for histories and masters.

sentences.zh: 又經義中選之文多膚淺，乞擇學官，及本科人充試官。

translations.literal: Moreover, writings that pass classical exegesis are mostly superficial; we beg to select school officials and men of that subject to serve as examiners.'
translations.idiomatic: Classical-exegesis passes were often shallow; they asked to appoint school officials and specialists as examiners.'

sentences.zh: 」省臣謂：「若不與本傳，恐碩學者有偶忘之失，可令但知題意而已。

translations.literal: ' Provincial ministers said: 'If source passages are not given, learned men may occasionally forget and be wrongly failed; let it suffice that they know the topic's meaning.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Provincial ministers replied: 'Without source passages, learned men might forget references and fail unfairly; requiring knowledge of the topic should suffice.'

sentences.zh: 」遂命擇前經義進士為眾所推者、才識優長者為學官，遇差考試官之際，則驗所治經參用。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon it was ordered to choose former classical-exegesis jinshi whom the multitude recommended and men of superior talent and insight as school officials; when assigning examination officials, verify the classic each had studied and employ accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: ' The court then appointed former exegesis jinshi whom peers respected and men of superior talent as school officials, and when assigning examiners matched them to the classics they had mastered.

sentences.zh: 詞賦進士，題注本傳，不得過五十字。

translations.literal: For rhapsody jinshi, source passages noted under questions could not exceed fifty characters.
translations.idiomatic: For rhapsody jinshi, source citations under questions could not exceed fifty characters.

sentences.zh: 經義進士，禦試第二場，試論日添試策一道。

translations.literal: For classical-exegesis jinshi, at the palace examination second round, on the day of testing essays one policy question was added.
translations.idiomatic: For exegesis jinshi, the palace examination's second round added one policy essay on the day of the composition test.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，上諭宰臣曰：「一場放二狀元，非是。

translations.literal: In Chengan 4 the emperor instructed the chief ministers: 'Granting two top graduates in one round is not right.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan 4 (1199) the emperor told his ministers: 'Naming two top graduates in one examination is wrong.

sentences.zh: 後場廷試，令詞賦、經義通試時務策，止選一狀元，余雖有明經、法律等科，止同諸科而已。

translations.literal: In the later palace examination round, order rhapsody and classical exegesis to be jointly tested on current-affairs policy essays, selecting only one top graduate; although there are also such subjects as classics mastery and law, they rank only with the other subjects.'
translations.idiomatic: In the palace round, rhapsody and exegesis candidates should sit a joint current-affairs policy test and yield only one top graduate; classics and law degrees rank with other subjects.'

sentences.zh: 」至宋王安石為相，作新經，始以經義取人。

translations.literal: ' By Song, when Wang Anshi became chief minister and composed new classics, recruitment by classical exegesis began.
translations.idiomatic: ' Under the Song, when Wang Anshi became chief minister and issued new classics, recruitment by exegesis began.

sentences.zh: 且詞賦、經義、人素所習之本業，策論則兼習者也。

translations.literal: Moreover, rhapsody and classical exegesis are the basic studies men have long practiced; policy essays are a supplementary study.
translations.idiomatic: Rhapsody and exegesis are candidates' primary training; policy essays are supplementary.

sentences.zh: 今舍本取兼習，恐不副陛下公選之意。

translations.literal: Now abandoning the basic for the supplementary study may not accord with Your Majesty's intent of impartial selection.'
translations.idiomatic: Favoring the supplementary over the primary may not match Your Majesty's intent of impartial selection.'

sentences.zh: 」遂定禦試同日各試本業，詞賦依舊，分立甲次，第一名為狀元，經義魁次之。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon it was fixed that on the same day of the palace examination each tested his own subject; rhapsody as before, with separate grades; first place was top graduate, classical-exegesis leader second.
translations.idiomatic: ' The court ruled that palace candidates test their own subject on the same day; rhapsody kept its former grading, with one top graduate and the exegesis leader second.

sentences.zh: 恩例與詞賦第二人同，餘分為兩甲中下人，並在詞賦之下。

translations.literal: Grace-precedent graduates ranked with the second rhapsody graduate; the rest were divided into two lower grades, all below rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Grace-precedent graduates ranked with the second rhapsody place; the rest formed two lower grades beneath rhapsody graduates.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔考試詞賦官各作程文一道，示為舉人之式，試後赴省藏之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year an edict ordered rhapsody examiners each to compose one model paper as the pattern for candidates, deposited in the province after the examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year examiners were ordered to compose one model rhapsody paper each as a pattern for candidates, deposited with the province after the exam.

sentences.zh: 時宰臣奏：「自大定二十五年以前，詞賦進士不過五百人，二十八年以不限人數，取至五百八十六人。

translations.literal: The chief ministers then memorialized: 'Before Dading 25, rhapsody jinshi did not exceed five hundred; in the twenty-eighth year, with no limit on numbers, five hundred eighty-six were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers reported: 'Before Dading 25, rhapsody jinshi never exceeded 500; in year 28, with no quota, 586 passed.

sentences.zh: 先承聖訓合格則取，故承安二年取九百二十五人。

translations.literal: Following the prior imperial instruction to take all who qualified, in Chengan 2 nine hundred twenty-five were taken.'
translations.idiomatic: Following the prior order to take all who qualified, Chengan 2 produced 925 graduates.'

sentences.zh: 兼今有四舉終場恩例，若會試取人數過多，則涉氾濫。

translations.literal: Moreover, today there is grace precedent for completing four examination rounds; if the metropolitan examination takes too many, it will verge on dilution.'
translations.idiomatic: With grace precedent for men who complete four examination cycles, too many metropolitan passes would dilute the degree.'

sentences.zh: 」遂定策論、詞賦、經義人數，雖多不過六百人，少則聽其闕。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon quotas were fixed for policy-essay, rhapsody, and classical-exegesis numbers: even if many, not more than six hundred; if few, vacancies were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: ' Quotas were set for policy-essay, rhapsody, and exegesis graduates: at most 600 even in abundant years; shortfalls were permitted.

sentences.zh: 時太常丞郭人傑轉對言，詞賦舉人，不得作別名兼試經義，及入學生精加試選，無至濫補。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Guo Renjie, in rotation memorializing, said rhapsody candidates must not use alternate names to also test classical exegesis, and school entrants should be strictly tested and selected so there would be no indiscriminate admission.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Guo Renjie argued that rhapsody candidates must not sit exegesis under alternate names and that school admission should be strictly tested to prevent indiscriminate enrollment.

sentences.zh: 上敕宰臣曰：「近已奏定，後場詞賦經義同日試之。

translations.literal: The emperor commanded the chief ministers: 'It was recently memorialized and fixed that in the later round rhapsody and classical exegesis would be tested on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his ministers: 'We recently ordered rhapsody and exegesis tested on the same day in the later round.

sentences.zh: 若府會試更不令兼試，恐試經義者少，是虛設此科也。

translations.literal: If prefectural and metropolitan examinations no longer allow combined testing, I fear few will test classical exegesis, and this subject would be set up in vain.'
translations.idiomatic: If prefectural and metropolitan exams forbid combined testing, few will take exegesis and the subject becomes meaningless.'

sentences.zh: 別名之弊，則當禁之。

translations.literal: The abuse of alternate names should be prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: The abuse of alternate names must be banned.

sentences.zh: 補試入學生員，已有舊條，恐行之滅裂爾，宜嚴防閑。

translations.literal: Trial admission of school students already has old regulations; I fear they are executed loosely; supervision should be strict.'
translations.idiomatic: Trial school admission already has regulations, but they may be loosely enforced; supervision should be tightened.'

sentences.zh: 」張行簡轉對言：「擬作程文，本欲為考試之式，今會試考試官、禦試讀卷官皆居顯職，擢第後離筆硯久，不復常習，今臨試擬作之文，稍有不工，徒起謗議。

translations.literal: ' Zhang Xingjian, in rotation memorializing, said: 'Composing model papers was originally meant as the pattern for examinations; now metropolitan examiners and palace reading officials all hold eminent posts; after passing they have long left brush and ink and no longer practice regularly; model papers composed on the eve of testing, if slightly unpolished, only provoke criticism.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Zhang Xingjian argued: 'Model papers were meant as examination patterns, but metropolitan examiners and palace readers hold high office and no longer write regularly; last-minute models invite criticism if imperfect.'

sentences.zh: 」詔罷之。

translations.literal: ' An edict abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: ' An edict abolished the practice.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，平章政事徒單鎰病時文之弊，言：「諸生不窮經史，唯事末學，以致志行浮薄。

translations.literal: In Taihe 1 Grand Councilor Tushan Yi lamented the abuses of contemporary letters and said: 'Students do not exhaust the classics and histories, attending only to minor studies, so that purpose and conduct grow shallow.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 1 (1201) Grand Councilor Tushan Yi deplored contemporary literary fashion: 'Students neglect classics and histories for minor studies, and purpose and conduct grow shallow.

sentences.zh: 可令進士試策日，自時務策外，更以疑難經旨相參為問，使發聖賢之微旨、古今之事變。

translations.literal: Let jinshi on the day of testing policy essays, besides current-affairs questions, also be questioned with difficult points from the classics interwoven, so they may unfold the subtle meaning of sages and the changes of affairs ancient and modern.'
translations.idiomatic: On policy-essay day, besides current affairs, add difficult classical questions so candidates unfold sage subtleties and historical change.'

sentences.zh: 」詔為永制。

translations.literal: ' An edict made this a permanent regulation.
translations.idiomatic: ' An edict made this permanent.

sentences.zh: 先嘗敕樂人不得舉進士，而奴免不良者則許之。

translations.literal: Previously it had been commanded that musicians could not take jinshi examinations, yet freed slaves of bad character were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians had been barred from jinshi examinations, yet freed slaves of bad character were allowed to test.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏：「舊稱工樂，謂配隸之色及倡優之家。

translations.literal: The Secretariat memorialized: 'The old term artisan-musician referred to tattooed bondsmen and families of actors.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat replied: 'The old term artisan-musician meant tattooed bondsmen and actors' families.

sentences.zh: 今少府監工匠，太常大樂署樂工，皆民也，而不得與試。

translations.literal: Today artisans of the Palace Storehouse Directorate and musicians of the Grand Music Office of the Imperial Sacrifices are all commoners, yet may not take the examinations.'
translations.idiomatic: Today's Palace Storehouse artisans and Imperial Sacrifices musicians are commoners, yet cannot test.'

sentences.zh: 前代令諸選人身及祖、父曾經免為良者，雖在官不得居清貫及臨民，今反許試，誠玷清論。

translations.literal: Former dynasties ordered that for all selectees, if they or their ancestors or fathers had once been freed to commoner status, even if in office they could not hold pure ranks or govern the people; now they are permitted to test—this truly stains pure discourse.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties barred selectees whose ancestors had been freed slaves from pure ranks or governing the people; allowing them to test now stains the system's reputation.'

sentences.zh: 」詔遂定制，放良人不得應諸科舉，其子孫則許之。

translations.literal: ' An edict then fixed the regulation: freed commoners may not take any examinations; their descendants are permitted.
translations.idiomatic: ' An edict fixed the rule: freed slaves may not test, but their descendants may.

sentences.zh: 上又謂：「德行才能非進士科所能盡，可通行保舉之制。

translations.literal: The emperor also said: 'Virtue, conduct, talent, and ability are not fully encompassed by the jinshi subject; the system of recommendation and guarantee may be broadly applied.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said: 'Virtue and talent exceed what the jinshi examinations can measure; broaden the recommendation system.'

sentences.zh: 省奏：「在《周禮》，'大司徒以鄉三物教萬民而賓興之。

translations.literal: The province memorialized: 'In the Rites of Zhou, the Grand Minister of Education taught the myriad people with the three village teachings and raised them as guests.'
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat replied: 'The Rites of Zhou says the Grand Minister of Education taught the people with the three village teachings and raised worthy men as guests.'

sentences.zh: 」所謂萬民，農工商賈皆是也。

translations.literal: ' The so-called myriad people includes farmers, artisans, merchants, and traders all.
translations.idiomatic: ' The myriad people included farmers, artisans, merchants, and traders alike.

sentences.zh: 前代立賢無方，如版築之士、鼓刀之叟，垂光簡策者不可勝舉。

translations.literal: Former ages established worthies without fixed method; men who built walls, old men who sharpened knives—those who shine in the records cannot be fully enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier dynasties recruited talent without fixed method; wall-builders and knife-grinders whose names shine in the records are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 今草澤隱逸才行兼備者，令謀克及司縣舉，按察司具聞，以旌用之，既有已降令文矣。

translations.literal: Today for recluses in the wilds with both conduct and talent, order mouke and circuit-prefecture counties to recommend, investigation commissions to report fully, and honor and employ them—there are already issued commands.'
translations.idiomatic: Today recluses of talent and character should be recommended by mouke and county officials, reported by investigation commissions, and honored in office—decrees to this effect already exist.'

sentences.zh: 」上命複宣旨以申之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor ordered the edict proclaimed again to reinforce it.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor ordered the decree proclaimed again.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐二年，禦史台言：「明年省試以中都、遼東、西北京等路道阻，宜於中都、南京兩處試之。

translations.literal: In Zhenyou 2 under Emperor Xuanzong, the Censorate said: 'Next year's provincial examination—because routes to Zhongdu, Liaodong, Western and Eastern Beijing, and other circuits are obstructed—it should be held at Zhongdu and Nanjing only.'
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzong's Zhenyou 2 (1214) the Censorate urged holding the next provincial examination only at Zhongdu and Nanjing because routes to Liaodong and other circuits were blocked.

sentences.zh: 」三年，諭宰臣曰：「國初設科，素號嚴密，今聞會試至於雜坐喧嘩，何以防弊？

translations.literal: ' In the third year he instructed the chief ministers: 'When the dynasty first established subjects, they were known as strict; now I hear that at the metropolitan examination candidates sit mixed together in noisy clamor—how is fraud to be prevented?'
translations.idiomatic: ' In the third year he told his ministers: 'Early examinations were famously strict; now metropolitan candidates sit mingled and noisy—how can fraud be prevented?'

sentences.zh: 」命治考官及監察罪。

translations.literal: ' He ordered examiners and supervisors punished.
translations.idiomatic: ' He ordered examiners and supervisors punished.

sentences.zh: 興定二年，禦史中丞把胡魯言：「國家數路收人，惟進士之選最為崇重，不求備數，惟務得賢。

translations.literal: In Xingding 2 Censor-in-Chief Ba Hulu said: 'The state recruits men by many routes, but only jinshi selection is most honored; it does not seek to fill quotas, only to obtain the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingding 2 (1218) Censor-in-Chief Ba Hulu said: 'The state recruits through many channels, but only jinshi selection is most honored; it seeks worthies, not quotas.

sentences.zh: 今場會試，策論進士不及二人取一人，詞賦、經義二人取一，前雖有聖訓，當依大定之制，中選即收，無問多寡，然大定間赴試者或至三千，取不過五百。

translations.literal: Now at the metropolitan examination, policy-essay jinshi take fewer than one in two, rhapsody and classical exegesis one in two; though there was formerly an imperial instruction, the Dading system should be followed—if they pass, take them regardless of number; yet in the Dading era those who presented themselves sometimes reached three thousand, and no more than five hundred were taken.'
translations.idiomatic: Now policy-essay jinshi pass at less than one in two, rhapsody and exegesis at one in two. Though an earlier imperial order said to take all who qualified, Dading practice is the model: three thousand might present themselves, yet only five hundred passed.'

sentences.zh: 泰和中，策論進士三人取一，詞賦、經義四人取一，向者貞祐初，詔免府試，赴會試者幾九千人。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, policy-essay jinshi were one in three, rhapsody and classical exegesis one in four; earlier at the beginning of Zhenyou, prefectural examination was waived, and those who came to the metropolitan examination were nearly nine thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taihe, policy-essay jinshi passed one in three, rhapsody and exegesis one in four. Early in Zhenyou prefectural exams were waived and nearly nine thousand came to the metropolitan round.

sentences.zh: 而取八百有奇，則是十之一而已。

translations.literal: Yet only a little over eight hundred were taken—only one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Only a little over eight hundred passed—one in ten.

sentences.zh: 時已有依大定之制，亦何嘗二人取一哉！

translations.literal: Even then, though following the Dading system, when was it ever one in two!
translations.idiomatic: Even then, following Dading practice, passes were never as loose as one in two!

sentences.zh: 今考官氾濫如此，非所以為求賢也。

translations.literal: Now examiners are so lax—this is not the way to seek the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Examiners are now so lax—that is not how to seek talent.

sentences.zh: 宜於會試之前，奏請所取之數，使恩出於上可也。

translations.literal: Before the metropolitan examination, the number to be taken should be memorialized and requested, so that favor issues from above.'
translations.idiomatic: The quota should be memorialized before the metropolitan examination so the throne sets the number.'

sentences.zh: 」詔集文資官議，卒從泰和之例。

translations.literal: ' An edict assembled civil officials for discussion, and in the end the Taihe precedent was followed.
translations.idiomatic: ' Civil officials were assembled for debate, and the Taihe precedent was adopted.

sentences.zh: 又謂宰臣曰：「從來廷試進士，日晡後即遣出宮，恐文思遲者不得盡其才，令待至暮時。

translations.literal: He also told the chief ministers: 'From of old palace-examination jinshi were sent out of the palace after the hour of shen; I fear slow writers could not exhaust their talent—let them wait until dusk.'
translations.idiomatic: He also told his ministers: 'Palace examinees were formerly dismissed after mid-afternoon; slow writers could not finish—let them remain until dusk.'

sentences.zh: 」特賜經義進士王彪等十三人及第，上覽其程文，愛其辭藻，咨歎久之。

translations.literal: ' Classical-exegesis jinshi Wang Biao and thirteen others were specially granted degrees; the emperor read their examination papers, loved their diction, and sighed in admiration for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thirteen exegesis graduates including Wang Biao received special degrees; the emperor read their papers, admired their diction, and sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 因怪學者益少，謂監試官左丞高汝礪曰：「養士學糧，歲稍豐熟即以本色給之，不然此科且廢矣！

translations.literal: Wondering that scholars grew fewer, he told Examination Supervisor Left Vice Minister Gao Ruli: 'Student grain rations—when the year is somewhat abundant, give it in kind; otherwise this subject will be abolished!'
translations.idiomatic: Noting that scholars were dwindling, he told Examination Supervisor Left Vice Minister Gao Ruli: 'Pay student grain rations in kind in good harvest years, or this degree track will die out!'

sentences.zh: 」五年，省試經義進士，考官于常格外多取十餘人，上命以特恩賜第。

translations.literal: ' In the fifth year, at the provincial examination for classical-exegesis jinshi, examiners took more than ten beyond the usual quota; the emperor ordered degrees granted by special grace.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the fifth year exegesis examiners took more than ten beyond quota; the emperor granted them special-grace degrees.

sentences.zh: 又命河北舉人今府試中選而為兵所阻者，免後舉府試。

translations.literal: He also ordered that Hebei candidates who this year passed the prefectural examination but were blocked by troops be exempted from the next prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei candidates who passed prefectural exams this year but were blocked by troops were exempted from the next prefectural round.

sentences.zh: 策論進士，選女直人之科也。

translations.literal: Policy-essay jinshi were the subject for selecting Jurchen people.
translations.idiomatic: Policy-essay jinshi were the examination track for Jurchen recruitment.

sentences.zh: 始大定四年，世宗命頒行女直大小字所譯經書。

translations.literal: It began in Dading 4, when Emperor Shizong ordered the promulgation of classics translated into large and small Jurchen script.
translations.idiomatic: It began in Dading 4 (1164), when Shizong ordered issuance of classics in large and small Jurchen script.

sentences.zh: 每謀克選二人習之。

translations.literal: From each mouke two were chosen to study them.
translations.idiomatic: Each mouke chose two men to study them.

sentences.zh: 尋欲興女直字學校，猛安謀克內多擇良家子為生，諸路至三千人。

translations.literal: Soon they wished to establish Jurchen-script schools; within meng'an and mouke many sons of good families were chosen as students, reaching three thousand on all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Schools in Jurchen script followed; meng'an and mouke units enrolled many sons of respectable families, reaching three thousand empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 九年，選異等者百人，薦于京師，廩給之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, one hundred of outstanding grade were chosen, recommended to the capital, and given grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the hundred most outstanding students were sent to the capital with state rations.

sentences.zh: 命溫蒂罕締達教以古書，作詩、策，後復試，得徒單鎰以下三十餘人。

translations.literal: Wendihan Dida was ordered to teach them ancient books; they composed poems and policy essays; tested again later, more than thirty including Tushan Yi passed.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Dida taught them classical texts; after further testing more than thirty passed, including Tushan Yi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，始議行策選之制，至十三年始定每場策一道，以五百字以上成，免鄉試府試，止赴會試禦試。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year discussion began on implementing policy selection; by the thirteenth year it was fixed that each round had one policy essay of five hundred characters or more, exempting district and prefectural examinations—only metropolitan and palace examinations were taken.
