translations.idiomatic: In year 11 the court debated policy selection; by year 13 each round required one policy essay of at least 500 characters, with district and prefectural rounds waived—only metropolitan and palace exams remained.

sentences.zh: 且詔京師女直國子學，諸路設女直府學，擬以新進士充教授，以教士民子弟之願學者。

translations.literal: An edict also established the Jurchen Directorate in the capital and Jurchen prefectural schools on all circuits, intending newly made jinshi as instructors to teach sons of officers and commoners who wished to study.
translations.idiomatic: The court also founded a Jurchen Directorate in the capital and Jurchen prefectural schools, staffed by new jinshi to teach willing sons of officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 俟行之久學者眾，則同漢進士三年一試之制。

translations.literal: When the system had long been in place and scholars were many, it would follow the Han jinshi system of testing once every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Once the system matured and enrollment grew, it would follow the Han jinshi cycle of examinations every three years.

sentences.zh: 乃就憫忠寺試徒單鎰等，其策曰：「賢生於世，世資於賢，世未嘗不生賢，賢未嘗不輔世。

translations.literal: Then at Bao'en Temple Tushan Yi and others were tested; his policy essay said: 'The worthy are born in the world, and the world relies on the worthy; the world has never failed to produce worthies, and worthies have never failed to assist the world.
translations.idiomatic: At Bao'en Temple Tushan Yi and others were tested. His policy essay began: 'The worthy are born into the world, and the world depends on them; the world never lacks worthies, and worthies never fail to serve the world.

sentences.zh: 蓋世非無賢，惟用與否。

translations.literal: The world is not without worthies—only whether they are used or not.
translations.idiomatic: The world is never without worthies—only whether rulers employ them.

sentences.zh: 若伊尹之佐成湯，傅說之輔高宗，呂望之遇文王，皆起耕築漁釣之間，而其功業卓然，後世不能企及者，蓋殷、周之君能用其人，盡其才也。

translations.literal: Such as Yi Yin assisting Cheng Tang, Fu Yue assisting Gaozong, Lü Wang meeting King Wen—all rose from plowing, building, fishing, and angling, yet their achievements were outstanding and later ages cannot approach them, because the rulers of Yin and Zhou could employ such men and exhaust their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Yin served Cheng Tang, Fu Yue Gaozong, and Lü Wang King Wen—all rose from farming, building, fishing, and angling to achievements later ages cannot match, because Yin and Zhou rulers employed their talents fully.

sentences.zh: 本朝以神武定天下，聖上以文德綏海內，文武並用，言小善而必從，事小便而不棄，蓋取人之道盡矣！

translations.literal: Our dynasty by martial spirit settled the realm; the sage emperor by civil virtue pacifies within the seas; civil and martial are both employed; speaking a small good he surely follows, a small matter he does not discard—the way of obtaining men is complete!
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty conquered by martial prowess; the sage emperor governs by civil virtue; civil and martial talents are both used; the throne heeds even small good counsel and does not dismiss small tasks—the method of recruiting men is complete!

sentences.zh: 而尚憂賢能遺於草澤者，今欲盡得天下之賢用之，又俾賢者各盡其能，以何道而臻此乎？

translations.literal: Yet he still worries that talent remains abandoned in the wilds; now wishing to obtain all the realm's worthies and employ them, and also to make worthies each exhaust their ability—by what path may this be reached?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court still fears talent abandoned in obscurity. How may every worthy in the realm be found, employed, and enabled to give his full ability?

sentences.zh: 」憫忠寺舊有雙塔，進士入院之夜半，聞東塔上有聲如音樂，西入宮。

translations.literal: At Bao'en Temple there were formerly twin pagodas; at midnight on the night the jinshi entered the examination hall, sound like music was heard atop the eastern pagoda, then passed west into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bao'en Temple had long had twin pagodas. At midnight on the night the jinshi entered the hall, music-like sounds were heard from the eastern pagoda and drifted westward into the palace.

sentences.zh: 考試官侍御史完顏蒲涅等曰：「文路始開而有此，得賢之祥也。

translations.literal: The examination officials, Censor Wanyan Pu'nie and others, said: 'The literary path has just opened and this has occurred—it is an auspicious omen of obtaining worthies.'
translations.idiomatic: The chief examiners, led by Censor Wanyan Pu'nie, declared: 'The civil service route has only just opened, and this is an auspicious sign that worthy men will be found.'

sentences.zh: 」中選者得徒單鎰以下二十七人。

translations.literal: Those selected numbered twenty-seven, including Tushan Yi and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven candidates passed, headed by Tushan Yi.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命皇家兩從以上親及宰相子，直赴禦試。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, it was ordered that imperial clansmen of the second degree of mourning and above, and sons of chancellors, proceed directly to the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 the court ordered imperial kinsmen within the second degree of mourning and sons of chancellors to skip preliminary rounds and go straight to the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 皇家袒免以上親及執政官之子，直赴會試。

translations.literal: Sons of imperial clansmen of the fifth degree of mourning and above and sons of executive officials proceed directly to the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of imperial kinsmen within the fifth degree of mourning and sons of chief ministers were allowed to proceed directly to the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 至二十年，以徒單鎰等教授中外，其學大振。

translations.literal: By the twentieth year, with Tushan Yi and others instructing inside and outside the court, learning flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: By year 20, with Tushan Yi and others teaching throughout the realm, Jurchen learning flourished.

sentences.zh: 遂定制，今後以策、詩試三場，策用女直大字，詩用小字，程試之期皆依漢進士例。

translations.literal: Regulations were then fixed: henceforth three rounds of policy essay and poetry would be tested; policy essays use large Jurchen script, poetry small script, and the examination schedule all follows Han jinshi precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations were then set: three rounds of policy essays and poetry; policy essays in large Jurchen script, poetry in small script; and the examination calendar would follow the Han jinshi model.

sentences.zh: 省臣奏：「漢人進士來年三月二十日鄉試，八月二十日府試，次年正月二十日會試，三月十二日禦試。

translations.literal: Provincial officials memorialized: 'Han jinshi next year will have the district examination on the twentieth day of the third month, the prefectural on the twentieth of the eighth month, the metropolitan on the twentieth of the first month of the following year, and the palace on the twelfth of the third month.'
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials reported that Han jinshi examinations the following year would run district on the 20th of the third month, prefectural on the 20th of the eighth month, metropolitan on the 20th of the first month of the year after, and palace on the 12th of the third month.

sentences.zh: 」敕以來年八月二十五日於中都、上京、咸平、東平府等路四處府試，餘從前例。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the prefectural examination on the twenty-fifth of the eighth month of the coming year at four locations—the Central Capital, Upper Capital, Xianping, and Dongping circuits; the rest follow previous precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict set the prefectural examination for the 25th of the eighth month of the coming year at four sites—Central Capital, Upper Capital, Xianping, and Dongping—while other dates followed earlier practice.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「契丹文字年遠，觀其所撰詩，義理深微，當時何不立契丹進士科舉，今雖立女直字科，慮女直字創制日近，義理未如漢字深奧，恐為後人議論。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Khitan script has existed for many years; viewing poems composed in it, their meaning is profound and subtle. Why did they not establish Khitan jinshi examinations then? Though we now establish a Jurchen-script degree, I worry Jurchen script was created only recently and its meaning is not as deep and abstruse as Chinese characters—I fear later generations will criticize this.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Khitan writing is ancient; poems in it show subtle meaning. Why was no Khitan jinshi degree established then? We now have a Jurchen-script track, but Jurchen script is newly invented and may not match the depth of Chinese—I fear later critics.'

sentences.zh: 」丞相守道曰：「漢文字恐初亦未必能如此。

translations.literal: Chancellor Shoudao said: 'Chinese script in its beginning probably could not yet do this either.'
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Shoudao replied: 'Chinese writing probably could not have reached such depth at first either.'

sentences.zh: 由歷代聖賢漸加修舉也。

translations.literal: It was through successive generations of sages gradually cultivating and elevating it.
translations.idiomatic: Successive sages refined it over generations.

sentences.zh: 聖主天姿明哲，令譯經教天下，行之久亦可同漢人文章矣！

translations.literal: The sage lord is naturally wise and enlightened; he has ordered the classics translated to teach the realm—with long practice it can equal Han literary compositions!
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor is naturally wise; he has ordered the classics translated for the realm—with time Jurchen writing can equal Han literature!

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「其同漢人進士例。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'It shall follow Han jinshi precedent.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Let it follow Han jinshi precedent.'

sentences.zh: 譯作程文，俾漢官覽之。

translations.literal: Translate the examination papers so Han officials may review them.
translations.idiomatic: Exam papers shall be translated for Han officials to review.

sentences.zh: 」二十二年三月，策試女直進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, third month, policy examination for Jurchen jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 22, third month, the Jurchen jinshi policy examination was held.

sentences.zh: 至四月癸丑，上謂宰臣曰：「女直進士試已久矣，何尚未考定？

translations.literal: By the fourth month, day guichou, the emperor said to his ministers: 'The Jurchen jinshi examination ended long ago—why has grading not yet been finalized?'
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day in the fourth month the emperor asked his ministers: 'The Jurchen jinshi exam ended ages ago—why are results still unsettled?'

sentences.zh: 」參知政事斡特剌對曰：「以其譯付看故也。

translations.literal: Vice Director Wateci replied: 'Because translations are being sent out for review.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wateci answered: 'Because the papers are still being translated for review.'

sentences.zh: 」上令速之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered it expedited.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them to hurry.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，上曰：「女直進士設科未久，若令積習精通，則能否自見矣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the emperor said: 'The Jurchen jinshi degree was established not long ago; once accumulated practice brings mastery, ability or inability will show itself.'
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the emperor said: 'The Jurchen jinshi track is still new; once candidates have trained long enough, talent will reveal itself.'

sentences.zh: 」二十八年，諭宰臣曰：「女直進士惟試以策，行之既久，人能預備，今若試以經義可乎？

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he instructed the ministers: 'Jurchen jinshi are tested only with policy essays; this has gone on long enough that people can prepare in advance. Would it be suitable now to test classics-meaning?'
translations.idiomatic: In year 28 he told his ministers: 'Jurchen jinshi have been tested only on policy essays; after so long, candidates can prepare. Should we add classics-meaning?'

sentences.zh: 」宰臣對曰：「《五經》中《書》、《易》、《春秋》已譯之矣，俟譯《詩》 、《禮》畢，試之可也。

translations.literal: The ministers replied: 'Among the Five Classics, the Documents, Changes, and Spring and Autumn Annals have already been translated; once the Poetry and Rites are finished translating, testing may begin.'
translations.idiomatic: The ministers answered: 'Documents, Changes, and Spring and Autumn are already translated; once Poetry and Rites are done, classics-meaning testing would be feasible.'

sentences.zh: 」 上曰：「大經義理深奧，不加歲月不能貫通。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The great classics' meaning is deep and abstruse; without years one cannot master them thoroughly.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'The great classics are profound; mastery requires years of study.'

sentences.zh: 今宜於經內姑試以論題，後當徐試經義也。」

translations.literal: For now we should tentatively test with discourse topics drawn from the classics; later we shall gradually test classics-meaning.'
translations.idiomatic: For now let us test discourse topics drawn from the classics; classics-meaning can come later.'

sentences.zh: 章宗大定二十九年，詔許諸人試策論進士舉。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong, Dading twenty-ninth year, edicted permission for all people to take the policy-and-discourse jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29, Emperor Zhangzong opened the policy-and-discourse jinshi examination to all subjects.

sentences.zh: 七月，省奏：「如詩、策、論俱作一日程試，恐力有不逮。

translations.literal: Seventh month, the provincial memorial said: 'If poetry, policy, and discourse are all scheduled for one day, candidates may not have strength enough.'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month provincial officials reported: 'Scheduling poetry, policy, and discourse all in one day may exceed candidates' stamina.'

sentences.zh: 詩、策作一日，論作一日，以詩、策合格為中選，而以論定其名次。

translations.literal: Poetry and policy on one day, discourse on another; passing poetry and policy qualifies for selection, and discourse determines rank.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry and policy would be tested on one day, discourse on another; passing poetry and policy would qualify a candidate, with discourse determining rank.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「論乃新添，至第三舉時當通定去留。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Discourse is newly added; by the third examination cycle it should fully determine pass and fail.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Discourse is new; by the third examination cycle it should fully determine who passes and fails.'

sentences.zh: 」明昌元年，猛安謀克願試進士者擬依餘人例，不可令直赴禦試。

translations.literal: Mingchang first year: mian'an and mukun wishing to take the jinshi examination should follow others' precedent and not be allowed to proceed directly to the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 1, mian'an and mukun candidates wishing to take the jinshi exam were to follow ordinary rules and could not skip straight to the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「是止許女直進士，毋令試漢進士也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'This only permits Jurchen jinshi—do not allow them to take Han jinshi examinations.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor clarified: 'This applies only to the Jurchen jinshi track—they must not take Han jinshi examinations.'

sentences.zh: 」又定制，餘官第五品散階，令直赴會試，官職俱至五品，令直赴禦試。

translations.literal: Regulations were also fixed: other officials holding fifth-rank dispersal rank may proceed directly to the metropolitan examination; those whose official posts all reach fifth rank may proceed directly to the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: New rules also allowed other officials of fifth-rank dispersal status to go directly to the metropolitan exam, and those whose posts all ranked fifth rank or above to go directly to the palace exam.

sentences.zh: 承安二年，敕策論進士限丁習學。

translations.literal: Cheng'an second year, an edict limited household adult males for policy-and-discourse jinshi study.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 2 an edict imposed household quotas on who could study for the policy-and-discourse jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 遂定制，內外官員、諸局分承應人、武衛軍、若猛安謀克女直及諸色人，戶止一丁者不許應試，兩丁者許一人，四丁二人，六丁以上止許三人。

translations.literal: Regulations were then fixed: inner and outer officials, clerks of various bureaus, palace guards, mian'an-mukun Jurchen, and persons of all categories—households with only one adult male may not take the examination; two males permit one; four permit two; six or more permit at most three.
translations.idiomatic: Rules were set for officials, bureau clerks, palace guards, mian'an-mukun Jurchen, and all other groups: one adult male per household barred from the exam; two males allowed one candidate; four allowed two; six or more capped at three.

sentences.zh: 三次終場，不在驗丁之限。

translations.literal: Those completing three full examination cycles are exempt from household-quota verification.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who had completed three full examination cycles were exempt from household-quota checks.

sentences.zh: 三年，定制，女直人以年四十五以下，試進士舉，于府試十日前，委佐貳官善射者試射。

translations.literal: Third-year regulations: Jurchen under forty-five taking the jinshi examination, ten days before the prefectural exam, deputy officials skilled in archery conduct an archery test.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 rules were set: Jurchen candidates under forty-five taking the jinshi exam would be archery-tested ten days before the prefectural round by deputy officials skilled in shooting.

sentences.zh: 其制，以六十步立垛，去射者十五步對立兩竿，相去二十步，去地二丈，以繩橫約之。

translations.literal: The method: at sixty paces set a target mound; fifteen paces from the archer stand two poles facing each other twenty paces apart, two zhang above the ground, bound with a horizontal rope.
translations.idiomatic: The setup placed a target mound at sixty paces; fifteen paces from the archer stood two poles twenty paces apart and two zhang high, spanned by a horizontal rope.

sentences.zh: 弓不限強弱，不計中否，以張弓巧便、發箭迅正者為熟閑。

translations.literal: Bow strength was unrestricted; hits were not counted—skill was judged by deft drawing and swift, straight release.
translations.idiomatic: Bow strength did not matter and hits were not scored; proficiency was judged by smooth drawing and a swift, straight release.

sentences.zh: 射十箭中兩箭，出繩下至垛者為中選。

translations.literal: Of ten arrows, hitting two that passed below the rope down to the mound qualified for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Of ten shots, two arrows passing below the rope and reaching the mound qualified a candidate.

sentences.zh: 余路委提刑司，在都委監察體究。

translations.literal: Other circuits delegated to judicial commissioners; in the capital, censorial investigators were charged with oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Other circuits delegated oversight to judicial commissioners; in the capital censors conducted investigations.

sentences.zh: 如當赴會試禦試者，大興府佐貳官試驗，三舉終場者免之。

translations.literal: Those proceeding to metropolitan and palace examinations were tested by Daxing prefectural deputies; those completing three full cycles were exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates bound for metropolitan and palace exams were tested by Daxing prefectural deputies; those who had completed three full cycles were exempt.

sentences.zh: 四年，禮部尚書賈鉉言：「策論進士程試弓箭，其兩舉終場及年十六以下未成丁者，若以弓箭退落，有失賢路。

translations.literal: Fourth year, Minister of Rites Jia Xuan said: 'Policy-and-discourse jinshi archery in the examination schedule—those completing two full cycles and those under sixteen not yet adult males, if failed by archery, would lose talented candidates from the path.'
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Minister of Rites Jia Xuan argued: 'Requiring archery in the policy-and-discourse jinshi schedule may eliminate worthy men who have completed two full cycles or youths under sixteen not yet counted as adult males.'

sentences.zh: 乞於及第後試之，中者別加任使，或升遷，否者降之。

translations.literal: He requested testing after passing the degree; those who passed would receive special appointments or promotion, others demotion.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that archery be tested after degree conferral, with successful shooters given special appointments or promotion and failures demoted.

sentences.zh: 」省臣謂：「舊制三舉終場免試，今兩舉亦免之，未可。

translations.literal: Provincial officials said: 'The old system exempted those completing three full cycles; now exempting two is not acceptable.'
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials replied: 'The old rule exempted those who completed three full cycles; exempting after only two would be too lenient.'

sentences.zh: 若以未成丁免試，必有妄匿年者，如果幼，使徐習未晚也。

translations.literal: If non-adults were exempted, some would falsely conceal their age; if truly young, gradual practice would not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Exempting non-adults would invite false age claims; truly young candidates could train and try again later.

sentences.zh: 至於及第後試驗升降，則已有定格矣。

translations.literal: As for post-degree testing with promotion or demotion, fixed regulations already existed.
translations.idiomatic: As for post-degree archery testing with promotion or demotion, fixed rules already existed.

sentences.zh: 」詔從舊制。

translations.literal: An edict followed the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict upheld the old regulations.

sentences.zh: 在泰和格，複有以時務策參以故事，及疑難經旨為問之制。

translations.literal: In the Taihe statutes there were also regulations mixing current-affairs policy with precedents and difficult classics questions.
translations.idiomatic: The Taihe code also provided for policy questions on current affairs mixed with precedents and difficult passages from the classics.

sentences.zh: 宣宗南遷，興定元年，制中都、西京等路，策論進士及武舉人權于南京、東平、婆速、上京四處府試。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuanzong's southward relocation, Xingding first year, regulations for the Central Capital, Xijing, and other circuits temporarily assigned policy-and-discourse jinshi and military examination candidates to prefectural examinations at Nanjing, Dongping, Basui, and Upper Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanzong moved south, in Xingding 1 candidates from the Central Capital, Xijing, and related circuits for policy-and-discourse jinshi and military exams were temporarily assigned to prefectural sites at Nanjing, Dongping, Basui, and Upper Capital.

sentences.zh: 五年，上賜進士斡勒業德等二十八人及第。

translations.literal: Fifth year, the emperor granted twenty-eight jinshi including Wolie Yede the degree.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 the emperor conferred degrees on twenty-eight jinshi, including Wolie Yede.

sentences.zh: 上覽程文，怪其數少，以問宰臣，對曰：「大定制隨處設學，諸謀克貢三人或二人為生員，贍以錢米。

translations.literal: The emperor reviewed the examination papers and wondered at their small number; asking the ministers, they replied: 'Great Dading regulations established schools everywhere; each mukun sent two or three as students, provisioned with money and grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing the papers, the emperor was struck by how few candidates had passed and asked his ministers. They explained: 'Under Great Dading, schools were set up everywhere; each mukun sent two or three students supported with money and grain.'

sentences.zh: 至泰和中，人例授地六十畝。

translations.literal: By the Taihe period, each person was granted sixty mu of land by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: By the Taihe era each student was routinely granted sixty mu of land.

sentences.zh: 所給既優，故學者多。

translations.literal: Provisions being generous, scholars were many.
translations.idiomatic: Support was generous, so enrollment was large.

sentences.zh: 今京師雖存府學，而月給通寶五十貫而已。

translations.literal: Now though the capital prefectural school remains, the monthly allowance is only fifty strings of currency.
translations.idiomatic: Today the capital prefectural school survives, but monthly support is only fifty strings of currency.

sentences.zh: 若于諸路總管府、及有軍戶處置學養之，庶可加益。

translations.literal: If schools with support were established at circuit headquarters and where military households exist, numbers could increase.
translations.idiomatic: Establishing supported schools at circuit headquarters and where military households are stationed might increase enrollment.

sentences.zh: 京師府學已設六十人，乞更增四十人。

translations.literal: The capital prefectural school already had sixty—he requested forty more.
translations.idiomatic: The capital prefectural school already enrolled sixty; he asked for forty more places.

sentences.zh: 中京、亳州、京兆府並置學官於總府，以謀克內不隸軍籍者為學生，人畀地四十畝。

translations.literal: Zhongjing, Bozhou, and Jingzhao prefectures would all establish school officials at headquarters; mukun members not on military rolls would serve as students, each granted forty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing, Bozhou, and Jingzhao would each place school officials at headquarters, enrolling mukun members not on military rolls as students with forty mu of land apiece.

sentences.zh: 漢學生在京者亦乞同此，餘州府仍舊制。

translations.literal: Han students in the capital also requested the same treatment; other prefectures would follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Han students in the capital asked for the same benefits; other prefectures would keep the old system.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 凡會試之數，大定二十五年，詞賦進士不得過五百人。

translations.literal: As for metropolitan examination quotas, in Dading twenty-five rhymed-prose jinshi were not to exceed five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan examination quotas: in Dading 25 rhymed-prose jinshi were capped at five hundred.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，以不限人數，遂至五百八十六人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, with no limit on numbers, the total reached five hundred eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In year 28, with no cap, the number rose to five hundred eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 章宗令合格則取，故承安二年至九百二十五人。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong ordered taking all who passed, so in Cheng'an second year the number reached nine hundred twenty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhangzong ordered that all who passed be accepted, so in Cheng'an 2 the total reached nine hundred twenty-five.

sentences.zh: 時以複加四舉終場者，數太濫，遂命取不得過六百人。

translations.literal: Then, with four-time completers added back in, the numbers were too loose, so an order capped selections at six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Re-admitting four-time completers made the pool too large, so a cap of six hundred was imposed.

sentences.zh: 泰和二年，上命定會試諸科取人之數，司空襄言：「試詞賦、經義者多，可五取一。

translations.literal: Taihe second year, the emperor ordered fixing metropolitan quotas by subject; Sikong Xiang said: 'Rhymed-prose and classics-meaning candidates are many—take one in five.'
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2 the emperor ordered fixed metropolitan quotas by subject. Sikong Xiang proposed: 'Rhymed-prose and classics-meaning have many candidates—take one in five.'

sentences.zh: 策論絕少，可四取一。

translations.literal: Policy-and-discourse candidates are very few—take one in four.
translations.idiomatic: Policy-and-discourse candidates are scarce—take one in four.

sentences.zh: 恩榜本以優老於場屋者。

translations.literal: The grace list originally favored those aged in the examination halls.
translations.idiomatic: The grace list was originally meant to favor candidates long tested in the halls.

sentences.zh: 四舉受恩則太優，限以年則礙異材。

translations.literal: Granting grace after four attempts is too generous; limiting by age hinders exceptional talent.
translations.idiomatic: Grace after four attempts is too generous, but age limits would block late-blooming talent.

sentences.zh: 可五舉則授恩。

translations.literal: After five attempts grace may be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Grace should require five completed attempts.

sentences.zh: 」平章徒單鎰等言：「大定二十五年至明昌初，率三四人取一。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Tushan Yi and others said: 'From Dading twenty-five to early Mingchang, generally one in three or four was taken.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Tushan Yi and others noted: 'From Dading 25 to early Mingchang the rate was roughly one in three or four.'

sentences.zh: 」平章張汝霖亦言：「五人取一，府試百人中才得五耳。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin also said: 'One in five means of one hundred at the prefectural examination only five pass.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Zhang Rulin added: 'One in five means only five out of a hundred at prefectural level would pass.'

sentences.zh: 」遂定制，策論三人取一，詞賦、經義五人取一，五舉終場年四十五以上、四舉終場年五十以上者受恩。

translations.literal: Regulations were then fixed: policy-and-discourse one in three; rhymed-prose and classics-meaning one in five; those completing five full attempts aged forty-five or above, or four full attempts aged fifty or above, receive grace.
translations.idiomatic: Rules were set: policy-and-discourse one in three, rhymed-prose and classics-meaning one in five; grace went to those who completed five full cycles at age forty-five or above, or four at fifty or above.

sentences.zh: 凡考試官，大定間，府試六處，各差詞賦試官三員，策論試官二員。

translations.literal: As for examination officials, during the Dading period at six prefectural sites each had three rhymed-prose examiners and two policy-and-discourse examiners dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Examination officials: during Dading, six prefectural sites each received three rhymed-prose examiners and two policy-and-discourse examiners.

sentences.zh: 明昌初，增為九處，路各差九員，大興府則十一員。

translations.literal: Early Mingchang expanded to nine sites; each circuit received nine officials, Daxing eleven.
translations.idiomatic: Early Mingchang expanded to nine sites, nine examiners per circuit, eleven for Daxing.

sentences.zh: 承安四年，又增太原為十處。

translations.literal: Cheng'an fourth year added Taiyuan for ten sites.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 4 Taiyuan was added, making ten sites.

sentences.zh: 有司請省之，遂定策論進士女直經童千人以上差四員，五百人以上三員，不及五百二員。

translations.literal: The authorities requested reduction; it was then fixed that for policy-and-discourse jinshi and Jurchen child-examinations, one thousand or more candidates received four examiners, five hundred or more three, under five hundred two.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities asked to cut staff; quotas were set for policy-and-discourse jinshi and Jurchen child-exams—four examiners for one thousand or more candidates, three for five hundred or more, two for fewer than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 各以職官高者一人為考試官，餘為同考試官。

translations.literal: In each case the highest-ranking official served as chief examiner, the rest as associate examiners.
translations.idiomatic: The senior official served as chief examiner; the others were associate examiners.

sentences.zh: 詞賦進士與律科舉人共及三千以上五員，二千四員，不及二千三員。

translations.literal: Rhymed-prose jinshi and legal candidates combined: three thousand or more received five examiners, two thousand four, under two thousand three.
translations.idiomatic: For rhymed-prose jinshi and legal candidates combined: five examiners for three thousand or more, four for two thousand or more, three for fewer than two thousand.

sentences.zh: 經義進士及經童舉人千人四員，五百以上三員，百人以上二員，不及百人以詞賦考官兼之。

translations.literal: Classics-meaning jinshi and child-examination candidates: one thousand received four examiners, five hundred or more three, one hundred or more two; under one hundred rhymed-prose examiners doubled in duty.
translations.idiomatic: For classics-meaning jinshi and child-exams: four examiners for one thousand candidates, three for five hundred or more, two for one hundred or more; under one hundred, rhymed-prose examiners would serve double duty.

sentences.zh: 後又定制，策論試官，上京、咸平、東平各三員，北京、西京、益都各二員。

translations.literal: Later regulations fixed policy-and-discourse examiners: Upper Capital, Xianping, and Dongping three each; Beijing, Xijing, and Yidu two each.
translations.idiomatic: Later rules fixed policy-and-discourse examiners at three each for Upper Capital, Xianping, and Dongping, and two each for Beijing, Xijing, and Yidu.

sentences.zh: 律科，監試官一員，試律官二員，隸詞賦考試院。

translations.literal: For the legal subject: one supervising examiner, two legal examiners, subordinate to the rhymed-prose examination hall.
translations.idiomatic: Legal examinations had one supervising examiner and two legal examiners under the rhymed-prose examination hall.

sentences.zh: 經童，試官一員，隸經義考試院，與會試同。

translations.literal: For child-examinations: one examiner, subordinate to the classics-meaning examination hall, the same as at the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Child-exams had one examiner under the classics-meaning hall, matching metropolitan practice.

sentences.zh: 其彌封並謄錄官、檢搜懷挾官、自余修治試院、監押門官，並如會試之制。

translations.literal: Sealing officials, copy clerks, search officials for hidden notes, and all others maintaining the hall and guarding the gates followed metropolitan regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Sealing clerks, copyists, search officials, hall maintenance staff, and gate guards all followed metropolitan rules.

sentences.zh: 大定二十年，上以往歲多以遠地官考試不便，遂命差近者。

translations.literal: Dading twentieth year, the emperor noted that in past years distant officials as examiners caused inconvenience and ordered nearer appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 20 the emperor noted that appointing distant officials as examiners had caused hardship and ordered nearer officials chosen instead.

sentences.zh: 凡會試，知貢舉官、同知貢舉官，詞賦則舊十員，承安五年為七員。

translations.literal: For metropolitan examinations, chief and associate chief examiners for rhymed-prose were formerly ten, reduced to seven in Cheng'an fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: At metropolitan exams, chief and associate chief examiners for rhymed-prose had been ten, reduced to seven in Cheng'an 5.

sentences.zh: 經義則六員，承安五年省為四員。

translations.literal: For classics-meaning there were six, reduced to four in Cheng'an fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: Classics-meaning had six, cut to four in Cheng'an 5.

sentences.zh: 詮讀官二員。

translations.literal: Two interpreting examiners.
translations.idiomatic: Two interpreting examiners were appointed.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年，上以彌封官渫語于舉人，敕自今女直司則用右選漢人封，漢人司則以女直司封。

translations.literal: Taihe third year, because sealing officials leaked talk to candidates, an edict ordered that henceforth the Jurchen bureau use Han right-selection seals, and the Han bureau use Jurchen bureau seals.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3, after sealing officials leaked information to candidates, an edict required the Jurchen bureau to use Han right-selection seals and the Han bureau to use Jurchen seals.

sentences.zh: 宣宗貞祐三年，以會試賦題已曾出，而有犯格中選者，複以考官多取所親，不怒其不公，命究治之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, Zhenyou third year, because a metropolitan rhyme topic had already appeared and rule-violating candidates still passed—and examiners had favored their kin—unable to condone the unfairness, he ordered an investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 3 of Xuanzong's reign, a metropolitan rhyme topic had been reused yet rule-breaking candidates passed, and examiners had favored relatives; the emperor, angered by the unfairness, ordered an investigation.

sentences.zh: 凡禦試，讀卷官，策論、詞賦進士各七員，經義五員，餘職事官各二員。

translations.literal: For palace examinations, paper-reading officials numbered seven each for policy-and-discourse and rhymed-prose jinshi, five for classics-meaning, and two for each other functional post.
translations.idiomatic: At palace exams, paper readers numbered seven each for policy-and-discourse and rhymed-prose jinshi, five for classics-meaning, and two for each other functional category.

sentences.zh: 制舉宏詞共三員。

translations.literal: Decree examination and grand eloquence: three total.
translations.idiomatic: Decree examination and grand eloquence together had three readers.

sentences.zh: 泰和七年，禮部尚書張行簡言：「舊例，讀卷官不避親，至有親人，或有不敢定其去留，或力加營護，而為同列所疑。

translations.literal: Taihe seventh year, Minister of Rites Zhang Xingjian said: 'By old precedent paper readers need not avoid kin; when kin were present some dared not decide their fate, or exerted protection, arousing colleagues' suspicion.'
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 7 Minister of Rites Zhang Xingjian reported: 'By old rule readers need not avoid kin; when relatives appeared, some dared not judge them fairly, or protected them too openly, inviting colleagues' suspicion.'

sentences.zh: 若讀卷官不用與進士有親者，則讀卷之際得平心商確。

translations.literal: If paper readers related to jinshi were not used, reading could proceed with impartial consultation.
translations.idiomatic: If readers related to candidates were excluded, grading could proceed in impartial consultation.

sentences.zh: 」上遂命臨期多擬，其有親者汰之。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered extra nominations before the deadline, eliminating those with kin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered extra nominees prepared in advance and those with kin among candidates removed.

sentences.zh: 凡府試策論進士，大定二十年定以中都、上京、咸平、東平四處。

translations.literal: For prefectural policy-and-discourse jinshi examinations, Dading twentieth year fixed four sites: Central Capital, Upper Capital, Xianping, and Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural policy-and-discourse jinshi exams were fixed in Dading 20 at four sites: Central Capital, Upper Capital, Xianping, and Dongping.

sentences.zh: 至明昌元年，添北京、西京、益都為七處，兼試女直經童。

translations.literal: By Mingchang first year Beijing, Xijing, and Yidu were added for seven sites, also testing Jurchen child-examinations.
translations.idiomatic: By Mingchang 1 Beijing, Xijing, and Yidu were added for seven sites, which also hosted Jurchen child-exams.

sentences.zh: 凡上京、合懶、速頻、胡裏改、蒲與、東北招討司等路者，則赴會寧府試。

translations.literal: Those from the Upper Capital, Helan, Supin, Huligai, Puyu, Northeast Pacification Commissioner, and other circuits proceeded to the Huining prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from Upper Capital, Helan, Supin, Huligai, Puyu, the Northeast Pacification Commissioner, and related circuits took the Huining prefectural exam.

sentences.zh: 咸平、隆州、婆速、東京、蓋州、懿州者，則赴咸平府試。

translations.literal: Those from Xianping, Longzhou, Basui, Dongjing, Gaizhou, and Yizhou proceeded to the Xianping prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from Xianping, Longzhou, Basui, Dongjing, Gaizhou, and Yizhou took the Xianping prefectural exam.

sentences.zh: 中都、河北東西路者，則赴大興府試。

translations.literal: Those from the Central Capital and Hebei East and West circuits proceeded to the Daxing prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from the Central Capital and Hebei East and West circuits took the Daxing prefectural exam.

sentences.zh: 西京並西南、西北二招討司者，則赴大同府試。

translations.literal: Those from Xijing together with the Southwest and Northwest Pacification Commissioners proceeded to the Datong prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from Xijing and the Southwest and Northwest Pacification Commissioners took the Datong prefectural exam.

sentences.zh: 北京、臨潢、宗州、興州、全州者，則赴大定府試。

translations.literal: Those from Beijing, Linhuang, Zongzhou, Xingzhou, and Quanzhou proceeded to the Dading prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from Beijing, Linhuang, Zongzhou, Xingzhou, and Quanzhou took the Dading prefectural exam.

sentences.zh: 山東西、大名、南京者，則赴東平府試。

translations.literal: Those from Shandong East and West, Daming, and Nanjing proceeded to the Dongping prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from Shandong East and West, Daming, and Nanjing took the Dongping prefectural exam.

sentences.zh: 山東東路則試於益都。

translations.literal: Those from Shandong East circuit proceeded to the Yidu examination.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates from Shandong East circuit tested at Yidu.

sentences.zh: 凡詞賦、經義進士及律科、經童府試之處，大定間，大興、大定、大同、開封、東平、京兆凡六處。

translations.literal: For all rhapsody jinshi, classical exegesis jinshi, legal studies, and child classics prefectural examinations, during the Dading period there were six sites in total: Daxing, Dading, Datong, Kaifeng, Dongping, and Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: During Dading, prefectural exams for rhapsody and exegesis jinshi, legal studies, and child classics were held at six sites: Daxing, Dading, Datong, Kaifeng, Dongping, and Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明昌初，增遼陽，平陽，益都為九處。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingchang, Liaoyang, Pingyang, and Yidu were added, making nine sites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Mingchang, Liaoyang, Pingyang, and Yidu were added, bringing the total to nine sites.

sentences.zh: 承安四年複增太原為十。

translations.literal: In Cheng'an fourth year Taiyuan was again added, making ten.
translations.idiomatic: In Cheng'an 4 (1199) Taiyuan was added again, for ten sites in all.

sentences.zh: 中都、河北則試於大興府，上京、東京、咸平府等路則試于遼陽府，余各試於其境。

translations.literal: The Central Capital and Hebei tested at Daxing prefecture; Upper Capital, Eastern Capital, Xianping prefecture, and other circuits tested at Liaoyang prefecture; the rest each tested within their own territories.
translations.idiomatic: Central Capital and Hebei candidates tested at Daxing; Upper Capital, Eastern Capital, Xianping, and related circuits at Liaoyang; all other regions tested within their own jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 凡鄉試之期，以三月二十日。

translations.literal: The date for all district examinations was the twentieth day of the third month.
translations.idiomatic: District examinations were scheduled for the twentieth day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 府試之期，若策論進士則以八月二十日試策，間三日試詩。

translations.literal: For prefectural examinations, policy-and-discourse jinshi tested policy essays on the twentieth of the eighth month, with poetry three days later.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural exams opened with policy essays for policy-and-discourse jinshi on the twentieth of the eighth month, followed three days later by poetry.

sentences.zh: 詞賦進士則以二十五日試賦及詩，又間三日試策論。

translations.literal: Rhapsody jinshi tested rhapsody and poetry on the twenty-fifth, with policy essays three days after that.
translations.idiomatic: Rhapsody jinshi tested rhapsody and poetry on the twenty-fifth, then policy essays three days later.

sentences.zh: 經義進士又間詞賦後三日試經義，又三日試策。

translations.literal: Classical exegesis jinshi tested exegesis three days after the rhapsody round, then policy essays three days after that.
translations.idiomatic: Exegesis jinshi sat the exegesis exam three days after the rhapsody jinshi, with policy essays following three days later.

sentences.zh: 次律科，次經童，每場皆間三日試之。

translations.literal: Next came legal studies, then child classics; each round was separated by three days.
translations.idiomatic: Legal studies followed, then child classics; each round was held three days apart.

sentences.zh: 會試，則策論進士以正月二十日試策，皆以次間三日，同前。

translations.literal: At the metropolitan examination, policy-and-discourse jinshi tested policy essays on the twentieth of the first month; all subsequent rounds were three days apart, as before.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan exams opened with policy essays for policy-and-discourse jinshi on the twentieth of the first month, with the same three-day intervals as at the prefectural level.

sentences.zh: 禦試，則以三月二十日策論進士試策，二十三日試詩論，二十五日詞賦進士試賦詩論，而經義進士亦以是日試經義，二十七日乃試策論。

translations.literal: At the palace examination, policy-and-discourse jinshi tested policy essays on the twentieth of the third month; the twenty-third tested poetry and discourse; on the twenty-fifth rhapsody jinshi tested rhapsody, poetry, and discourse, while exegesis jinshi also tested exegesis that day; on the twenty-seventh policy essays were tested.
translations.idiomatic: Palace exams ran policy essays for policy-and-discourse jinshi on the twentieth of the third month, poetry and discourse on the twenty-third, rhapsody/poetry/discourse for rhapsody jinshi and exegesis for exegesis jinshi on the twenty-fifth, and policy essays on the twenty-seventh.

sentences.zh: 若試日遇雨雪，則候晴日。

translations.literal: If rain or snow fell on an examination day, they waited for clear weather.
translations.idiomatic: Examination days postponed for rain or snow until the skies cleared.

sentences.zh: 禦試唱名後，試策則稟奏，宏詞則作二日程試。

translations.literal: After the palace examination roll call, policy-essay candidates reported and submitted memorials; eloquence candidates were given a two-day schedule for testing.
translations.idiomatic: After the palace roll call, policy-essay candidates submitted memorial reports, while eloquence candidates received a two-day examination schedule.

sentences.zh: 舊制，試女直進士在再試漢進士後。

translations.literal: Under the old system, Jurchen jinshi were examined after Han jinshi were re-examined.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Jurchen jinshi were tested only after Han jinshi completed their second round.

sentences.zh: 大定二十九年以複設經義科，更定是制。

translations.literal: In Dading twenty-ninth year the exegesis subject was re-established, and this system was revised.
translations.idiomatic: When the exegesis subject was restored in Dading 29 (1189), this arrangement was revised.

sentences.zh: 恩例。

translations.literal: Grace precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Grace Precedents.

sentences.zh: 明昌元年，定制，省元直就禦試，不中者許綴榜未。

translations.literal: In Mingchang first year regulations were set: metropolitan first-place winners proceeded directly to the palace examination; those who failed were permitted to be appended at the end of the list.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchang 1 (1190) rules allowed metropolitan winners straight into the palace exam, with failures appended to the bottom of the rolls.

sentences.zh: 解元但免府試，四舉終場依五舉恩例，所試文卷惟犯禦名廟諱、不成文理者則黜之，余並以文之優劣為次。

translations.literal: Prefectural first-place winners were only exempt from the prefectural examination; four-time completers followed five-time grace precedent; examination papers were rejected only if they violated imperial or ancestral taboos or lacked coherence—all others were ranked by literary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural winners skipped only the prefectural round; four-time completers received five-time grace benefits; papers were failed only for taboo violations or incoherence, with all others ranked by quality.

sentences.zh: 仍一日試三題，其五舉者止試賦詩，女直進士亦同此例。

translations.literal: They still tested three questions in one day; five-time candidates tested only rhapsody and poetry; Jurchen jinshi followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates still answered three questions in one day; five-time completers tested only rhapsody and poetry, as did Jurchen jinshi.

sentences.zh: 承安五年，敕進士四舉該恩，詞賦、經義當以各科為場數，不得通數。

translations.literal: In Cheng'an fifth year an edict held that jinshi who completed four examinations earned grace; for rhapsody and exegesis, session counts were tracked separately by subject and could not be combined.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'an 5 (1200) decreed that four completed attempts earned grace; rhapsody and exegesis session counts had to be tracked separately by subject, not combined.

sentences.zh: 又恩榜人應授官者，監試官于試時具數以奏，特恩者授之。

translations.literal: Also, for grace-list candidates due for office, supervising examiners reported their numbers at test time; specially graced candidates received appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising examiners reported grace-list appointees during testing, and special-grace candidates received their posts.

sentences.zh: 泰和三年，以經義會元與策論詞賦進士不同，若禦試被黜則附榜末，為太優，若同恩例，又與四舉者不同。

translations.literal: In Taihe third year, because exegesis metropolitan winners differed from policy-and-discourse and rhapsody jinshi, attaching them at the roll's end if failed at the palace exam was too generous; treating them like other grace cases also differed from four-time candidates.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 (1203), exegesis metropolitan winners differed from policy-and-discourse and rhapsody jinshi; appending palace failures to the roll's end was unduly generous, yet grace rules also differed from the four-time standard.

sentences.zh: 遂定制，依曾經府試解元免府試之例。

translations.literal: Regulations were then set following the precedent whereby prefectural first-place winners who had already taken the prefectural exam were exempt from it.
translations.idiomatic: New rules followed the established precedent exempting former prefectural winners from repeating the prefectural round.

sentences.zh: 會試下第，再舉直赴禦試。

translations.literal: Those who failed the metropolitan examination, on a second attempt proceeded directly to the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan failures on their next attempt went straight to the palace exam.

sentences.zh: 律科進士，又稱為諸科，其法以律令內出題，府試十五題，每五人取一人。

translations.literal: Legal studies jinshi, also called the miscellaneous subjects, drew questions from statutes and ordinances; the prefectural exam had fifteen questions, taking one in five.
translations.idiomatic: Legal-studies jinshi—also called the miscellaneous subjects—drew questions from law codes; prefectural exams had fifteen questions with one pass per five candidates.

sentences.zh: 大定二十二年定制，會試每場十五題，三場共通三十六條以上，文理優、擬斷當、用字切者，為中選。

translations.literal: Regulations set in Dading twenty-second year: the metropolitan exam had fifteen questions per session, three sessions totaling thirty-six correct answers or more; those with superior writing, apt judgments, and precise terminology passed.
translations.idiomatic: Dading 22 (1182) rules set fifteen questions per metropolitan session across three sessions; candidates passing at least thirty-six items with strong prose, sound judgments, and precise language were selected.

sentences.zh: 臨時約取之，初無定數。

translations.literal: Numbers were taken approximately at the time; initially there was no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Quotas were set flexibly at the time; no fixed number existed initially.

sentences.zh: 其制始見於海陵庶人正隆元年，至章宗大定二十九年，有司言：「律科止知讀律，不知教化之源，可使通治《論語》、《孟子》，以涵養其氣度。

translations.literal: This system first appears in the first year of Zhenglong under the Deposed Emperor of Hailing; by Emperor Zhangzong's Dading twenty-ninth year officials said: 'Legal studies candidates know only how to read law and not the source of moral transformation—they should be made to study the Analects and Mencius to cultivate their bearing.'
translations.idiomatic: The system first appears in Hailing's Zhenglong 1 (1156); in Dading 29 (1189) under Emperor Zhangzong officials reported: 'Legal-studies candidates know statutes but not the moral foundations of governance—they should study the Analects and Mencius to cultivate their character.'

sentences.zh: 」遂令自今舉後，複於《論語》、《孟子》內試小義一道，府會試別作一日引試，命經義試官出題，與本科通考定之。

translations.literal: An order was then issued that from the next examination onward, one short exegesis question from the Analects and Mencius would again be tested; prefectural and metropolitan exams would hold a separate day for this supplementary test, with exegesis examiners setting questions and grading jointly with the main subject.
translations.idiomatic: From the next round onward, one short exegesis question from the Analects and Mencius was added on a separate day at prefectural and metropolitan exams, set by exegesis examiners and graded together with the legal-studies papers.

sentences.zh: 經童科

translations.literal: The Child Classics Subject
translations.idiomatic: The Child Classics Subject

sentences.zh: 經童之制，凡士庶子年十三以下，能誦二大經、三小經，又誦《論語》諸子及五千字以上，府試十五題通十三以上，會試每場十五題，三場共通四十一以上，為中選。

translations.literal: The child classics system: any commoner or gentry child aged thirteen or below who could recite two major classics and three minor classics, also recite the Analects, various masters, and five thousand characters or more; at the prefectural exam fifteen questions with thirteen or more passed; at the metropolitan exam fifteen questions per session, three sessions totaling forty-one or more passed—such candidates were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Under the child-classics system, boys aged thirteen or under who could recite two major and three minor classics, the Analects, selected masters, and over five thousand characters passed the prefectural round by answering at least thirteen of fifteen questions, and the metropolitan round by scoring at least forty-one across three sessions of fifteen questions each.

sentences.zh: 所貴在幼而誦多者，若年同，則以誦大經多者為最。

translations.literal: What was prized was reciting much while young; if ages were equal, the one who recited more major classics ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Youth and breadth of recitation were prized; when ages matched, the candidate who had recited more major classics ranked first.

sentences.zh: 初，天會八年時，太宗以東平童子劉天驥，七歲能誦《詩》、《書》、《易》、《禮》、《春秋左氏傳》及《論語》、《孟子》，上命教養之，然未有選舉之制也。

translations.literal: Initially, in the eighth year of Tianhui, Emperor Taizong, seeing the Dongping child Liu Tianji, aged seven, able to recite the Odes, Documents, Changes, Rites, Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, Analects, and Mencius, ordered him nurtured in learning—yet there was no examination system.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, in Tianhui 8 (1130), Emperor Taizong learned that Liu Tianji, a seven-year-old boy from Dongping, could recite the Odes, Documents, Changes, Rites, Zuo Commentary, Analects, and Mencius, and ordered him placed under tutelage—but no examination system yet existed.

sentences.zh: 熙宗即位之二年，詔辟貢舉，始備其列，取至百二十二人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Xizong's accession, an edict opened recruitment examinations; the category was first fully established, selecting as many as one hundred twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Xizong's reign (1147), an edict opened recruitment examinations; the child-classics track was formally established, selecting up to 122 candidates.

sentences.zh: 天德間，廢之。

translations.literal: During the Tiande period it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished during the Tiande era (1149–1153).

sentences.zh: 章宗大定二十九年，上謂宰臣曰：「經童豈遽無人，其議複置。

translations.literal: In Dading twenty-ninth year under Emperor Zhangzong, the emperor told his chief ministers: 'Can child classics truly have no candidates so soon? Discuss restoring it.'
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29 (1189) Emperor Zhangzong told his chief ministers: 'Surely child-classics candidates cannot have vanished entirely—discuss restoring the subject.'

sentences.zh: 」明昌元年，益都府申：「童子劉住兒年十一歲，能詩賦，誦大小六經，所書行草頗有法，孝行夙成，乞依宋童子李淑賜出身，且加以恩詔。

translations.literal: In Mingchang first year Yidu prefecture reported: 'The child Liu Zhu'er, aged eleven, can compose poetry and rhapsody, recite all six classics major and minor, writes running and cursive script with considerable skill, and filial conduct matured early—we beg that he be granted office following the Song child Li Shu's precedent, and additionally receive an imperial grace edict.'
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 1 (1190) Yidu prefecture reported: 'Liu Zhu'er, aged eleven, can compose poetry and rhapsody, recite all six classics, writes running and cursive script with real skill, and has shown filial conduct from early youth—we ask that he receive office as did the Song prodigy Li Shu, together with an imperial grace edict.'

sentences.zh: 」召至內殿，試《鳳凰來儀》賦、《魚在藻》詩，又令賦《旱》詩，上嘉之，賜本科出身，給錢粟官舍，令肄業太學。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the inner hall and tested on the rhapsody 'The Phoenix Comes with Auspicious Bearing' and the poem 'Fish amid the Waterweeds'; he was also ordered to compose a poem on drought. The emperor praised him, granted him graduation in this subject, provided money, grain, and official quarters, and ordered him to study at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the inner hall, he was tested on the rhapsody 'The Phoenix Comes with Auspicious Bearing' and the poem 'Fish amid the Waterweeds,' then asked to compose a poem on drought. The emperor praised him, granted child-classics graduation, supplied money, grain, and official quarters, and enrolled him at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年，平章政事完顏守貞言：「經童之科非古也，自唐諸道表薦，或取五人至十人。

translations.literal: In Mingchang third year Grand Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen said: 'The child classics subject is not ancient; from Tang onward circuits submitted memorial recommendations, taking from five to ten persons.'
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 3 (1192) Grand Councilor Wanyan Shouzhen said: 'The child-classics subject is not ancient; from Tang onward circuits submitted recommendations, selecting anywhere from five to ten candidates.'

sentences.zh: 近代宋仁宗以為無補，罷之。

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Renzong of Song deemed it useless and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Emperor Renzong of Song judged it useless and abolished it.

sentences.zh: 本朝皇統間取五十人，因以為常，天德時複廢。

translations.literal: In our dynasty during Huangtong fifty were taken, and this became regular practice; during Tiande it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under our dynasty fifty were selected during Huangtong (1141–1149), making that the norm, until Tiande abolished the subject again.

sentences.zh: 聖主複置，取以百數，恐久積多，不勝銓擬，乞諭旨約省取之。

translations.literal: The sage ruler restored it, taking them by the hundreds; I fear that over time the numbers will accumulate beyond what appointment review can bear—we beg an edict to limit and reduce selections.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty restored the subject and now selects by the hundreds; over time the numbers may overwhelm appointment review—we beg an edict to limit selections.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「若所誦皆及格，何如？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'If all who recite meet the standard, what then?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: 'What if every candidate who recites meets the standard?'

sentences.zh: 」守貞曰：「視最幼而誦不訛者精選之，則人數亦不至多也。

translations.literal: Shouzhen said: 'Select carefully those youngest who recite without error, and the numbers will not become excessive.'
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen replied: 'Choose carefully the youngest candidates who recite flawlessly, and the numbers need not grow excessive.'

sentences.zh: 」複問參知政事胥持國，對曰：「所誦通否易見，豈容有濫。

translations.literal: He again asked Vice Grand Councilor Xu Chiguo, who replied: 'Whether recitation is complete is easy to see—how could there be abuse?'
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Vice Grand Councilor Xu Chiguo, who answered: 'Whether a candidate's recitation is complete is easy to verify—abuse is hardly possible.'

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「限以三十或四十人，若百人皆通，亦可複取其精者。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Limit it to thirty or forty persons; if all one hundred pass, we may again select the finest among them.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Cap it at thirty or forty; if all one hundred pass, we can still choose the finest among them.'

sentences.zh: 」持國曰：「是科蓋資教之術耳。

translations.literal: Chiguo said: 'This subject is merely a method for nurturing education.'
translations.idiomatic: Chiguo said: 'This subject is essentially a tool for cultivating learning.'

sentences.zh: 夫幼習其文，長玩其義，使之蒞政，人格出焉。

translations.literal: When one studies the texts in youth and delights in their meaning in maturity, then upon entering governance a person's character emerges.
translations.idiomatic: Study the texts in youth, dwell on their meaning in maturity, and when such men enter office their character shows itself.

sentences.zh: 如中選者，加之修習進士舉業，則所記皆得為用。

translations.literal: If those selected additionally trained in jinshi examination work, all they had memorized would prove useful.
translations.idiomatic: If selected candidates also trained in jinshi examination work, everything they had memorized would become useful.

sentences.zh: 臣謂可勿令遽登仕途，必習舉業，而後官使之可也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that they should not be allowed to enter the official path too hastily; they must study examination work first, and only then be appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that they should not enter office too hastily; they must complete examination training before appointment.

sentences.zh: 若能擢進士第，自同進士任用。

translations.literal: If they could win jinshi rank, they would naturally be employed like jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Those who win jinshi rank should be employed on the same terms as other jinshi.

sentences.zh: 如中府薦或會試，視其次數，優其等級。

translations.literal: If they passed prefectural recommendation or the metropolitan exam, their number of attempts would be considered and their grade favored.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed prefectural recommendation or the metropolitan exam should receive preferential rank according to their number of attempts.

sentences.zh: 幾舉不得薦者，從本出身，似可以激勸而得人矣！

translations.literal: Those who after several attempts failed to gain recommendation would receive their original graduation status—this seems able to stimulate effort and win men of talent!
translations.idiomatic: Those who failed to gain recommendation after several attempts would retain their original child-classics status—this should spur effort and draw out real talent!

sentences.zh: 」詔議行之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered discussion and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the proposal discussed and put into effect.

sentences.zh: 制舉有賢良方正、能直言極諫、博學宏材、達于從政等科，試無常期。

translations.literal: Special recruitment included such subjects as Worthy and Upright, Straightforward Remonstrance, Broad Learning and Grand Talent, and Mastery of Governance; examinations had no fixed schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Special recruitment included Worthy and Upright, Straightforward Remonstrance, Broad Learning and Grand Talent, and Mastery of Governance; these exams had no fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 上意欲行，即告天下。

translations.literal: When the emperor's intent was to proceed, the realm was immediately notified.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to hold an exam, notice was issued throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 聽內外文武六品以下職官無公私過者，從內外五品以上官薦於所屬，詔試之。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials inside and outside the capital of rank six and below without public or private offenses were permitted, on recommendation by officials of rank five and above inside and outside the capital to their respective jurisdictions, to be tested by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of rank six and below without public or private offenses could be recommended by rank-five officials and above to their jurisdictions for imperial testing.

sentences.zh: 若草澤士，德行為鄉里所服者，則從府州薦之。

translations.literal: Common scholars whose conduct was respected in their villages were recommended through prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Common scholars whose conduct commanded local respect were recommended through prefectures and districts.

sentences.zh: 凡試，則先投所業策論三十道於學士院，視其詞理優者，委官以群經子史內出題，一日試論三道，如可，則庭試策一道，不拘常務，取其無不通貫者，優等遷擢之。

translations.literal: For all examinations, candidates first submitted thirty policy essays they had prepared to the Hanlin Academy; those whose language and reasoning were superior were assigned officials to set questions from the classics, masters, and histories; three essays were tested in one day; if qualified, one policy essay was tested in the hall examination without regard to routine affairs—those comprehensively versed were promoted in superior grade.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates first submitted thirty prepared policy essays to the Hanlin Academy; those judged strongest in language and reasoning were tested with three essay questions drawn from the classics, masters, and histories in one day; qualified candidates then faced one hall policy essay on non-routine matters, and those showing comprehensive mastery received superior promotion.

sentences.zh: 宏詞科試詔、誥、章、表、露布、檄書，則皆用四六；

translations.literal: The eloquence subject tested edicts, commissions, memorials, tables, battle bulletins, and proclamations—all in parallel prose;
translations.idiomatic: The eloquence subject tested edicts, commissions, memorials, tables, battle bulletins, and proclamations—all in parallel prose;

sentences.zh: 誡、諭、頌、箴、銘、序、記，則或依古今體，或參用四六。

translations.literal: Admonitions, instructions, eulogies, admonitory inscriptions, commemorative inscriptions, prefaces, and records might follow ancient or modern forms, or mix in parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: Admonitions, instructions, eulogies, admonitory inscriptions, commemorative inscriptions, prefaces, and records could follow ancient or modern forms, or mix in parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 于每舉賜第後進士及在官六品以下無公私罪者，在外官薦之，令試策官出題就考，通試四題，分二等遷擢之。

translations.literal: At each round, newly graduated jinshi and serving officials of rank six and below without public or private crimes were recommended by local officials; policy examiners set questions on the spot; four questions were tested in all, and promotion was divided into two grades.
translations.idiomatic: At each round, newly graduated jinshi and serving officials of rank six and below without public or private crimes could be recommended by local officials; policy examiners set questions on the spot for four questions total, with promotion divided into two grades.

sentences.zh: 二科皆章宗明昌元年所創者也。

translations.literal: Both subjects were created in Mingchang first year under Emperor Zhangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Both subjects were established in Mingchang 1 (1190) under Emperor Zhangzong.

sentences.zh: 武舉，嘗設于皇統時，其制則見於《泰和式》，有上中下三等。

translations.literal: Military examinations were once established during Huangtong; the system appears in the Taihe Regulations, with upper, middle, and lower grades.
translations.idiomatic: Military examinations were established during Huangtong; the rules appear in the Taihe Regulations, with upper, middle, and lower grades.

sentences.zh: 能挽一石力弓，以重七錢竹箭，百五十步立貼，十箭內，府試欲中一箭，省試中二箭，程試中三箭。

translations.literal: Able to draw a one-stone power bow, using bamboo arrows weighing seven qian; at one hundred fifty paces with a standing target; within ten arrows the prefectural exam required one hit, the provincial two, and the final round three.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates had to draw a one-stone bow and shoot seven-qian bamboo arrows at a standing target 150 paces away; within ten shots, the prefectural round required one hit, the provincial round two, and the final round three.

sentences.zh: 又遠射二百二十步垛，三箭內一箭至者。

translations.literal: Also long-range shooting at a mound two hundred twenty paces away, one of three arrows reaching it.
translations.idiomatic: They also had to hit a mound target at 220 paces, landing at least one of three arrows.

sentences.zh: 又百五十步內，每五十步設高五寸、長八寸臥鹿二，能以七斗弓、二大鑿頭鐵箭馳射，府試則許射四反，省試三反，程試二反，皆能中二箭者。

translations.literal: Also within one hundred fifty paces, at every fifty paces two prone deer targets five inches high and eight inches long were set; using a seven-dou bow and two large chisel-headed iron arrows while riding, the prefectural exam allowed four passes, the provincial three, and the final round two—all requiring two hits.
translations.idiomatic: Within 150 paces, prone deer targets five inches high and eight inches long were placed every 50 paces; mounted candidates shot with a seven-dou bow and two large chisel-headed iron arrows—the prefectural round allowed four passes, the provincial three, and the final round two, each requiring two hits.

sentences.zh: 又百五十步內，每三十步，左右錯置高三尺木偶人戴五寸方板者四，以槍馳刺，府試則許馳三反，省試二反，程試三反，左右各刺落一板者。

translations.literal: Also within one hundred fifty paces, at every thirty paces four wooden dummy men three feet high wearing five-inch square boards were placed alternately left and right; charging with a spear, the prefectural exam allowed three passes, the provincial two, and the final round three—knocking off one board on each side.
translations.idiomatic: Within 150 paces, wooden dummy men three feet high with five-inch square boards were placed alternately left and right every 30 paces; mounted spear charges required knocking off one board on each side—the prefectural round allowed three passes, the provincial two, and the final round three.

sentences.zh: 又依廕例問律一條，又問《孫》、《吳》書十條，能說五者，為上等。

translations.literal: Also following the hereditary privilege precedent one legal article was questioned, and ten questions on the Sun and Wu military texts were asked; answering five qualified for the upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Following hereditary-privilege precedent, candidates also answered one legal question and ten questions on the Sun and Wu military texts; answering five qualified for the upper grade.

sentences.zh: 凡程試，若一有不中者，皆黜之。

translations.literal: For all final examinations, if any single event was failed, all were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: In the final round, failure in any single event meant rejection.

sentences.zh: 若射貼弓八斗，遠射二百一十步，射鹿弓六斗，《孫》、《吳》書十條通四，為中等。

translations.literal: If the standing-target bow was eight dou, long-range shooting two hundred ten paces, deer-shooting bow six dou, and four of ten Sun and Wu questions answered, this was the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: The middle grade required an eight-dou standing-target bow, 210-pace long-range shooting, a six-dou deer-shooting bow, and four correct answers on the Sun and Wu texts.

sentences.zh: 射貼弓七斗，遠射二百五步，射鹿弓五斗，《孫》、《吳》書十條通三，為下等。

translations.literal: Standing-target bow seven dou, long-range shooting two hundred five paces, deer-shooting bow five dou, three of ten Sun and Wu questions answered—this was the lower grade.
translations.idiomatic: The lower grade required a seven-dou standing-target bow, 205-pace long-range shooting, a five-dou deer-shooting bow, and three correct answers on the Sun and Wu texts.

sentences.zh: 解律、刺板，皆欲同前。

translations.literal: Legal interpretation and board-striking requirements were the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: Legal interpretation and board-striking requirements matched the upper-grade standards.

sentences.zh: 凡不知書者，雖上等為中，中則為下。

translations.literal: All who did not know books, though upper grade became middle, and middle became lower.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who failed the literary portion were demoted one grade—upper to middle, middle to lower.

sentences.zh: 凡試中中下，願再試者聽。

translations.literal: All who passed at middle or lower grade, if willing to test again, were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who passed at middle or lower grade were permitted to retest if they wished.

sentences.zh: 舊制，就試上等不中，不許再試中下等。

translations.literal: Under the old system, if one attempted the upper grade and failed, retesting at middle or lower grade was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, candidates who failed while attempting the upper grade could not retest at middle or lower grade.

sentences.zh: 泰和元年，定制，不分舊等，但從所願，試中則以三等為次。

translations.literal: In Taihe first year regulations were set: regardless of former grade, candidates tested as they wished; if they passed, the three grades ranked them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Taihe 1 (1201) rules allowed candidates to test at whichever grade they chose; passes were ranked within the three grades accordingly.

sentences.zh: 二年，省奏：「武舉程式當與進士同時，今年八月府試，欲隨路設考試所，臨期差官，恐以創立未見應試人數，遂權令各處就考之。

translations.literal: Second year, provincial officials memorialized: 'Military examination schedule should coincide with jinshi; this year's August prefectural exam—we wish to establish examination sites by circuit and assign officials at the deadline, but fear that because this is newly established we cannot yet see the number of candidates, and so temporarily order each locality to test on the spot.'
translations.idiomatic: In the second year provincial officials reported: 'Military exams should run concurrently with jinshi; for this August prefectural round we planned circuit examination sites with officials assigned at the deadline, but fearing uncertain turnout for a newly established system, we temporarily allowed each locality to test on the spot.'

sentences.zh: 」宣宗貞祐三年，同進士例，賜敕命章服。

translations.literal: In Zhenyuo third year under Emperor Xuanzong, following jinshi precedent, edict-commission robes and insignia were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuo 3 (1215) under Emperor Xuanzong, military graduates received edict commissions and insignia robes on the same terms as jinshi.

sentences.zh: 時以隨處武舉入試者，自非見居職任及已用於軍前者，令郡縣盡遣詣京師，別為一軍，以備緩急。

translations.literal: At the time, military examination candidates entering tests from various places, unless currently holding office or already deployed at the front, were ordered by prefectures and districts to be sent entirely to the capital, formed into a separate army for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, military examination candidates from across the realm—unless already in office or deployed at the front—were sent to the capital by prefectures and districts and formed into a separate army for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 其被薦而未授官者，亦量材任之。

translations.literal: Those recommended but not yet appointed were also assigned duties according to their ability.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended candidates not yet appointed were also assigned duties according to their ability.

sentences.zh: 元光二年，東京總帥紇石烈牙吾塔言：「武舉入仕，皆授巡尉軍轄，此曹雖善騎射，不曆行陣，不知軍旅，一旦臨敵，恐致敗事。

translations.literal: In Yuanguang second year, Eastern Capital commander He Shilie Yawuta said: 'Military examination entrants to office are all appointed patrol officers and military jurisdiction posts; though these men excel at riding and shooting, they have not experienced battle formations and do not know military affairs—once they face the enemy, I fear defeat will follow.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanguang 2 (1223) Eastern Capital commander He Shilie Yawuta said: 'Military graduates are all posted as patrol officers and garrison commanders; though skilled at riding and archery, they lack battlefield experience and know nothing of command—once they face the enemy, defeat seems likely.'

sentences.zh: 乞盡括付軍前為長校，俟有功則升之。

translations.literal: I beg that all be gathered and assigned to the front as senior officers, to be promoted after meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they all be assigned to the front as senior officers and promoted only after earning merit.

sentences.zh: 」宰臣奏：「國家設此科與進士等，而欲盡置軍中，非獎進人材之道。

translations.literal: Chief ministers memorialized: 'The state established this subject on equal footing with jinshi, yet to place all in the army is not the way to reward and advance talent.'
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers replied: 'The state established this subject on equal footing with jinshi; placing all graduates in the army is not the way to reward talent.'

sentences.zh: 」遂籍丁憂、待闕、去職者付之。

translations.literal: Those registered in mourning, awaiting appointment, or leaving office were then assigned.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, candidates in mourning, awaiting appointment, or between posts were assigned.

sentences.zh: 試學士院官

translations.literal: Examination of Hanlin Academy Officials
translations.idiomatic: Examination of Hanlin Academy Officials

sentences.zh: 試學士院官。

translations.literal: Examination of Hanlin Academy officials.
translations.idiomatic: Examination of Hanlin Academy officials.

sentences.zh: 大定二十八年，敕設科取士為學士院官。

translations.literal: In Dading twenty-eighth year an edict established a subject to select scholars as Hanlin Academy officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 28 (1188) an edict established an examination track to recruit Hanlin Academy officials.

sentences.zh: 禮部下太常，按唐典，初入學士院例先試，今若于進士已仕者，以隨朝六品，外路五品職事官薦，試製詔誥等文字三道，取文理優者充應奉。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites forwarded the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; according to Tang precedent, entry into the Hanlin Academy was customarily preceded by examination. Now, for jinshi already in office, rank-six officials at court and rank-five functional officials on outer circuits would recommend them; three documents such as edicts and commissions would be tested, and those superior in language and reasoning would serve as attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites consulted the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; by Tang precedent, Hanlin entry required prior examination. Serving jinshi recommended by rank-six court officials or rank-five circuit officials were tested on three documents such as edicts and commissions; those strongest in language and reasoning were appointed as academy attendants.

sentences.zh: 由是翰苑之選為精。

translations.literal: Hence selection for the Hanlin groves became refined.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin recruitment thereby became more selective.

sentences.zh: 明昌五年，以學士院撰文字人少，命尚書省訪有文采者勾取權試之。

translations.literal: In Mingchang fifth year, because the Hanlin Academy had too few men to draft documents, the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to seek men of literary talent, summon them, and provisionally test them.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingchang 5 (1194), with too few Hanlin drafters available, the Ministry of Revenue was ordered to seek men of literary talent, summon them, and test them provisionally.

sentences.zh: 司天、醫學試科

translations.literal: Astronomy Bureau and Medical Examination Subjects
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy Bureau and Medical Examination Subjects

sentences.zh: 凡司天臺學生，女直二十六人，漢人五十人，聽官民家年十五以上，三十以下試補。

translations.literal: For all Astronomy Bureau students, twenty-six Jurchen and fifty Han; official and common households aged fifteen or above and thirty or below were permitted to test for admission.
translations.idiomatic: The Astronomy Bureau enrolled twenty-six Jurchen and fifty Han students; men aged fifteen to thirty from official and common households could test for admission.

sentences.zh: 又三年一次，選草澤人試補。

translations.literal: Also once every three years, common scholars were selected to test for admission.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years, common scholars were also selected to test for admission.

sentences.zh: 其試之制，以《宣明曆》試推步，及《婚書》、《地理新書》試合婚、安葬，並《易》筮法，六壬課、三命五星之術。

translations.literal: The examination system tested calendrical calculation through the Xuanming Calendar, marriage compatibility and burial placement through the Marriage Book and New Book of Geography, together with Changes divination, liuren divination, and the arts of the three fates and five stars.
translations.idiomatic: Examinations tested calendrical calculation through the Xuanming Calendar, marriage compatibility and burial placement through the Marriage Book and New Book of Geography, together with Changes divination, liuren divination, and the arts of the three fates and five stars.

sentences.zh: 凡醫學十科，大興府學生三十人，餘京府二十人，散府節鎮十六人，防禦州十人，每月試疑難，以所對優劣加懲勸，三年一次試諸太醫，雖不系學生，亦聽試補。

translations.literal: For all ten medical subjects, Daxing prefecture had thirty students, other capital prefectures twenty, regular prefectures and military commissions sixteen, defensive prefectures ten; each month difficult cases were tested, with reward or punishment according to the quality of answers; once every three years all court physicians were tested—even those not enrolled as students were permitted to test for admission.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine was divided into ten specialties: Daxing prefecture enrolled thirty students, other capital prefectures twenty, regular prefectures and military commissions sixteen, and defensive prefectures ten. Each month difficult cases were tested, with rewards or punishments according to performance; every three years all court physicians were examined—even non-students could test for admission.
